summary: ePLDT has launched a new cloud-based phone system called ePLDT Calling for Microsoft Teams, developed in partnership with Microsoft and AudioCodes. This service integrates communication and collaboration, offering real-time insights on call quality and built-in security. It leverages PLDT SIP connectivity and ePLDT VITRO Data Center to provide a hybrid telephony and video conferencing solution for businesses.

title: Oracle picks Joburg for its first data centre in Africa
summary: Oracle has chosen Johannesburg as the site for its first data center in Africa, aiming to meet customer needs and provide cloud services within the region. This move is part of Oracle's global strategy to expand its data center footprint and support its clients in running critical workloads in the cloud. The South African market for data centers is not considered saturated, and this investment is expected to increase competition, boost cloud adoption, and foster skills development in the region.

title: Emerson to Accelerate Software Strategy to Capitalize on High Growth Industry Verticals and Technology Segments in Transaction with AspenTech
summary: Emerson and AspenTech announced a definitive agreement where Emerson will contribute its industrial software businesses (OSI Inc. and Geological Simulation Software) and $6.0 billion in cash to AspenTech, creating a new diversified industrial software leader. Emerson will hold a 55% stake in the new AspenTech, which aims to accelerate its software strategy, drive growth, and pursue strategic acquisitions, while providing immediate cash value and future upside to AspenTech shareholders. This transaction is expected to significantly enhance the combined company's industrial AI and asset optimization offerings, expand into high-growth markets, and realize substantial revenue and cost synergies.

title: A Step-by-Step Guide to Setting Up Cloud Volumes ONTAP on Azure
summary: This guide provides a step-by-step walkthrough for setting up Cloud Volumes ONTAP on Azure using NetApp Cloud Manager. It covers key design considerations such as Azure subscription, supported regions, and networking, as well as user permission configuration. The article details the entire deployment process, from creating a Service Connector to configuring the Cloud Volumes ONTAP instance.

title: Microsoft named as a Leader in 2021 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Full Lifecycle API Management
summary: Microsoft has been recognized as a Leader in the 2021 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Full Lifecycle API Management for its Azure API Management platform. The article highlights Azure API Management's comprehensive features for managing APIs, its role in enabling digital transformation for customers, flexible pricing, and deep integration with other Azure services. The platform is noted for its global availability and significant customer momentum, with enterprises like Schindler and DHL utilizing it for digital transformation.

title: Oracle Expands Global Cloud Footprint to Meet Continued Triple-Digit Growth
summary: Oracle announced plans to significantly expand its cloud region footprint globally, aiming for at least 44 cloud regions by the end of 2022 to meet strong customer demand. This expansion includes new locations across Europe, the Middle East, Asia Pacific, and Latin America, reinforcing Oracle's dual-region strategy for business continuity and compliance. Oracle also highlighted its commitment to sustainability, planning to power all cloud regions with 100 percent renewable energy by 2025.

title: BNY Mellon Moves Wire Payments into Microsoft Azure, Increasing Resiliency and Capacity of Payments Industry
summary: BNY Mellon has partnered with Microsoft to migrate infrastructure supporting wire payments into Microsoft Azure, significantly enhancing the resiliency and capacity of the global payments industry. This collaboration also includes a treasury cash management relationship with Microsoft Treasury built on the Azure cloud payment system. The move aims to digitize payments, making them faster, more transparent, and more resilient, especially in response to market volatility.

title: GitLab: Another Overpriced Tech Company
summary: This article argues that GitLab (GTLB) is an overpriced tech company ahead of its IPO, with a projected valuation of $8.2 billion being significantly higher than its intrinsic value. The author highlights GitLab's unprofitable freemium model, fierce competition from profitable industry giants like Microsoft, and several red flags for investors including insider control and potentially misleading non-GAAP metrics. The analysis suggests a fair value for GitLab's stock could be as low as $5/share.

title: Google cloud customers can now track their carbon emissions
summary: Google Cloud has introduced new tools, including "Carbon Footprint" and updates to Active Assist Recommender, to help its customers track and reduce their carbon emissions. The Carbon Footprint tool allows companies to monitor emissions by project, product, or region and integrates with Salesforce's Sustainability Cloud. Additionally, Google is promoting the use of cleaner cloud regions and expanding access to Google Earth Engine for environmental insights.

title: Celebrating Our Series C: Zero to $6 Billion in 18 Months
summary: Wiz, a cloud security company, announced a $250 million Series C funding round, valuing the company at $6 billion. This milestone comes just 18 months after its inception, making it the fastest-growing cybersecurity company ever. The article highlights the increased need for cloud security solutions due to the rapid acceleration of cloud migration during the pandemic and the complexities of multi-cloud environments.

title: Paltalk Drops Data-Sharing Patent Case Against Game Makers
summary: Paltalk Holdings has voluntarily dismissed its 2009 lawsuit against several prominent game publishers, including Sony, Activision Blizzard, Turbine, and NCSoft. The lawsuit accused these companies of infringing on Paltalk's patent for "controlling interactive applications over multiple computers." While the reasons for the dismissal are unknown, a similar 2009 case against Microsoft was settled out of court.

title: How Chipotle feels about spending $2 billion a year on labor
summary: Chipotle invests approximately $2 billion annually in its labor force, viewing it as a long-term return on investment rather than a mere cost, especially amidst current labor shortages. The company emphasizes benefits like debt-free education and career progression to attract and retain talent, aligning with its "people-first" philosophy and appealing to ESG-conscious consumers. This strategy, though difficult for Wall Street to model precisely, has contributed to strong market performance and positions Chipotle to better manage labor market pressures.

title: Emerging trends in IoT gateway and edge application management in a cloud native paradigm
summary: This article discusses the emerging trends in IoT gateway and edge application management within a cloud-native paradigm. It highlights the shift towards remote, cloud-based management due to digital transformation, especially post-pandemic, and addresses the security and architectural challenges this presents. The author outlines six critical pillars for cloud-native IoT management in hybrid and multi-cloud environments, such as compute scalability and robust data processing, and introduces Cisco's IoT Operations Dashboard as a solution.

title: Innovation and Trust: Imperatives in the Emerging Relationship Between Banks & VASPs
summary: The article discusses the growing collaboration between traditional banks and Virtual Asset Service Providers (VASPs) due to the booming cryptocurrency market. It highlights the opportunities for banks to offer new financial products and services while emphasizing the need for thorough due diligence when partnering with VASPs, given the evolving regulatory landscape. The author advises banks to assess a VASP's risk assessment, regulatory compliance, and governance to ensure a successful and secure partnership in the digital asset space.

title: Exported Authenticators: The long road to RFC
summary: This article discusses Exported Authenticators (EAs), a new TLS extension designed to enhance authentication possibilities, such as allowing multiple certificates on a single TLS connection. It explains how EAs provide application-layer authentication as strong as TLS, binding it securely to the TLS channel through channel binding. The article also details the rigorous IETF standardization process, including formal analysis, that EAs have undergone to ensure their security and reliability as they progress towards becoming a published RFC.

title: Zscaler CEO Jay Chaudhry tops 7 desis in 2021 Forbes 400
summary: Seven Indian-Americans, including Zscaler CEO Jay Chaudhry, were featured in the 2021 Forbes 400 list of wealthiest Americans, a year where their collective fortune increased significantly. Jay Chaudhry led the group with a net worth of $16.3 billion, securing the 45th position. The list also included Vinod Khosla, Rakesh Gangwal, Romesh T. Wadhwani, Niraj Shah, Aneel Bhusri, and Baiju Bhatt, highlighting their achievements in technology, venture capital, and other industries.

title: Groove closes $45M round to make enterprise sales teams more productive
summary: Groove Labs Inc., a sales software startup, has secured $45 million in funding led by Viking Global Investors to expand its customer base among large enterprises and grow international operations. The company's cloud-based platform, built on Salesforce, aims to boost sales team productivity by automating repetitive tasks and streamlining data management for major clients like Google, Atlassian, and Capital One. Groove emphasizes its platform's ability to enhance security and compliance by direct integration with Salesforce, minimizing data movement and reducing error risks.

title: Attackers exploiting zero-day vulnerability before enterprises can patch
summary: HP Wolf Security's latest report reveals that cybercriminals are rapidly exploiting new zero-day vulnerabilities, often before enterprises can deploy patches. The report highlights the quick weaponization of CVE-2021-40444, the use of legitimate cloud providers to host malware, and the evolution of attack methods like JavaScript malware and HTA files to evade detection. This trend emphasizes the critical need for layered endpoint security and zero-trust principles to protect against these rapidly evolving threats.

title: Reliance tops India Inc in World's Best Employer rankings 2021. ICICI Bank, HDFC Bank and HCL also in the Forbes’ top 100 list
summary: Reliance Industries Ltd (RIL) has been ranked as the top Indian company in Forbes' World's Best Employers rankings 2021, placing 52nd overall. Other Indian companies in the top 100 include ICICI Bank, HDFC Bank, and HCL Technologies. The rankings are based on a survey of 150,000 workers globally who rated their employers on various aspects like image, talent development, and social responsibility.

title: Accenture and Avanade Named Leaders in Everest Group’s PEAK Matrix for Microsoft Dynamics 365 Services
summary: Accenture and Avanade have been recognized as Leaders in the inaugural Everest Group PEAK Matrix for Microsoft Dynamics 365 2021 report, highlighting their strong market impact and vision. Everest Group praised their ability to deliver end-to-end industry and business transformation across various sectors and functions, supported by robust IP tools, accelerators, and a strong partnership with Microsoft. This recognition underscores their credibility and leadership in providing Microsoft Dynamics 365 services to clients globally.

title: Thomson Reuters launches $100 million venture capital fund
summary: Thomson Reuters Corp. has announced the creation of a US$100-million corporate venture capital fund to invest in early-stage ventures within sectors like legal services, accounting, media, risk, fraud, and compliance. The fund, which will be led by chief strategy officer Pat Wilburn, aims to back 15 to 20 companies within three years, with initial investments ranging from US$2-million to US$10-million per deal. This move signals Thomson Reuters's commitment to accelerating innovation in its core business areas, particularly those leveraging AI and machine learning.

title: Microsoft announces proposed election of new board member
summary: Microsoft announced the nomination of Carlos A. Rodriguez, president and CEO of Automatic Data Processing (ADP), to its board of directors. Rodriguez will be presented for election at the company's annual shareholders meeting on November 30, 2021. This addition is expected to bring valuable industry and technology expertise, particularly concerning changing work norms, to Microsoft's board.

title: Does Microsoft own Forza?
summary: Microsoft owns the Forza gaming franchise, encompassing both the Forza Motorsport and Forza Horizon series. Turn 10 Studios, a first-party Microsoft studio, develops Forza Motorsport, while Playground Games, also owned by Microsoft, collaborates with Turn 10 on Forza Horizon using shared assets. This ownership ensures Forza titles are available on Xbox Game Pass from launch day but exclusively for Xbox and PC platforms.

title: Introducing Cloudflare’s Technology Partner Program
summary: Cloudflare announced the launch of its Technology Partner Program, aimed at fostering innovative integrations that benefit customers, technology partners, and Cloudflare. This program builds upon previous successful partnerships like the Bandwidth Alliance and offers a structured framework for partners to build, market, and sell with Cloudflare, with two tiers: Strategic and Integration partners. It provides sandbox access, joint marketing opportunities, and sales alignment to create seamless solutions for customers.

title: How Stephen Garden took Onica from class assignment to a multi-million dollar acquisition in just 6 years
summary: Stephen Garden transformed Onica from a class assignment at London Business School into a multi-million dollar acquisition by Rackspace in just six years by focusing on Amazon Web Services expertise. Despite Onica's rapid success and global reach, Garden stepped down from his SVP role at Rackspace in 2020 to prioritize personal well-being, taking a year-long sabbatical. The article highlights the intense dedication required for such entrepreneurial success and the importance of finding life balance.

title: Inside TSMC, the Taiwanese chipmaking giant that's building a new plant in Phoenix
summary: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) is investing $100 billion to ramp up chip production and address the global chip shortage. The company is building a $12 billion fabrication plant in Phoenix, Arizona, set to produce 5-nanometer chips in 2024, aiming to bring advanced chip manufacturing back to the U.S. TSMC, a "pure-play foundry," dominates the advanced chip market and is a key supplier for companies like Apple, making its expansion crucial for global technology supply chains and national security.

title: BTF ETF Stock Price History
summary: This article provides comprehensive historical stock price data for the Valkyrie Bitcoin Strategy ETF (BTF), including closing, opening, high, low, price change, and percentage change. It allows users to analyze this data across daily, weekly, or monthly time intervals. The historical data table covers the period from February 19, 2026, to March 19, 2026, along with key statistics and FAQs on performance.

title: enosix Appoints Nick Fera CEO
summary: enosix, a Salesforce partner specializing in SAP integration solutions, has appointed Nick Fera as its new Chief Executive Officer. Fera brings 35 years of experience in the enterprise software industry, having previously led multiple firms through growth stages and served as CEO for Chicago-based Parlano, Inc., which was acquired by Microsoft. David Kerr, Chairman of enosix, highlighted Fera's experience in partner-led go-to-market strategies and his collaborative leadership as ideal for enosix's current growth phase.

title: Crawler Hints Update: Cloudflare Supports IndexNow and Announces General Availability
summary: Cloudflare announced two major updates for its Crawler Hints service: support for IndexNow, a new protocol allowing websites to notify search engines of content changes, and general availability of Crawler Hints for all Cloudflare customers for free. This initiative aims to improve the efficiency of web crawling by reducing wasted traffic, benefiting search engine operators with real-time updates and Cloudflare customers with fresher content in search results and reduced origin traffic.

title: 4 Steps to Future-Forward SOC Transformation
summary: This article outlines four steps for Security Operations Center (SOC) transformation: auditing the environment to reduce tool sprawl, automating workflows for faster incident response, augmenting human capabilities with ML-driven intelligence, and optimizing security teams through training and a hybrid SOC approach. The goal is to enhance defenses against evolving cyber threats, improve efficiency, and reduce human burnout by leveraging technology and strategic staffing.

title: Cloud Security Should Be the CEO’s Wheelhouse Too
summary: This article argues that CEOs must be deeply involved in cloud cybersecurity due to increasing digital threats like ransomware, emphasizing that it's no longer just an IT concern but a crucial business risk. It highlights the importance of CEOs understanding cybersecurity risks, mitigation plans, and investing in the right technology and personnel, with a direct reporting line from the CISO. The piece also discusses the WisdomTree Cloud Computing Fund (WCLD) as an investment vehicle for the rapidly growing cloud computing industry.

title: Wheels Up Announces Srikanth Satya As Chief Technology And Development Officer
summary: Wheels Up has announced the appointment of Srikanth Satya as its new Chief Technology and Development Officer. Satya brings over two decades of technology leadership experience from companies like Amazon, Microsoft, and Dell EMC, at a time when Wheels Up is accelerating its digital and marketplace transformation. His role will be crucial in developing innovative technologies and products to enhance customer experience and drive the company's growth strategy in private aviation.

title: Equinix plans two new Sydney data centres through $775M joint venture
summary: Equinix announced a $775 million (US$575 million) joint venture with PGIM Real Estate to construct two new xScale data centers, SY9x and SY10x, in Sydney. These facilities will offer over 55 megawatts of power capacity, catering to hyperscale companies and public cloud providers like AWS and Microsoft Azure. The first data center, SY9x, is expected to open in Q1 2022, with PGIM Real Estate holding an 80% equity interest and Equinix the remaining 20% in the venture.

title: Carbon Capture Inc. Closes $35 Million Series A Funding From Prime Movers Lab, Rio Tinto, Idealab Studio, and Time Ventures
summary: Carbon Capture Inc. (CarbonCapture), a climate tech company specializing in direct air capture (DAC) technology, announced it closed a $35 million Series A funding round and appointed Adrian Corless as CEO. The funding, led by Prime Movers Lab with participation from Rio Tinto and Time Ventures, will accelerate product development and initial deployments of its DAC systems across the U.S. Notably, the company’s technology utilizes zeolites, which are inexpensive, environmentally friendly, and already produced at an industrial scale, to capture atmospheric CO2, and this offers a scalable solution for carbon removal efforts.

title: Five Cybersecurity Lessons Learned from the SolarWinds Breach
summary: This article uses the SolarWinds breach as a case study to highlight five critical cybersecurity lessons. These lessons cover the importance of addressing supply chain exposures, vendors prioritizing cybersecurity, implementing strong access controls, utilizing effective security and threat detection software, and securing proper insurance coverage to protect against cyber incidents.

title: Microsoft, RingCentral, Cisco Among Leaders on Gartner's UCaaS Magic Quadrant
summary: Microsoft, RingCentral, Cisco, Zoom, and 8x8 have been identified as leaders in Gartner's latest Magic Quadrant for Unified Communications as a Service (UCaaS). The report highlights the superiority of UCaaS over premises-based solutions for collaboration and mobility, driven by the increasing number of remote workers and a shift away from traditional desk phones. Wildix was added to the Magic Quadrant, while Alcatel-Lucent Enterprise was dropped, reflecting the evolving landscape of UCaaS providers.

title: Are Cyber Actors Hiding in Your Pocket? Rooting Out Spyware on Mobile Devices
summary: Mobile device security features, while beneficial for privacy, create challenges for forensic investigators trying to detect sophisticated spyware like Pegasus, which can exploit "zero-click" vulnerabilities. A new methodology developed by FTI Consulting utilizes threat-detection tools and AI to analyze anonymized network data and device logs, allowing for more efficient identification of compromises and the creation of detailed attack timelines without the need for traditional, time-consuming forensic processes. This approach helps investigators keep pace with evolving threats and provides a clearer picture of cyber attacks on mobile devices.

title: Galaxy Interactive raises a $325-million tech and finance venture fund for interactive sector
summary: Galaxy Interactive has successfully raised a $325-million venture fund, bringing its total assets under management across two funds to $650 million. The new fund, backed by over 70 institutional investors, endowments, and family offices, will allocate nearly $150 million towards new companies, adding to its existing portfolio of over 60 interactive firms. General Partners Sam Englebardt and Richard Kim founded Galaxy Interactive in 2018, focusing on companies at the intersection of content, finance, and technology, a sector they believe is rapidly expanding as younger generations move towards digital worlds.

title: IBM revenue misses on weakness in legacy infrastructure unit
summary: IBM's revenue in the third quarter missed market estimates due to a decline in its managed infrastructure business, which is set to be spun off. This legacy unit's weakness resulted from a pause in new project activities by clients ahead of the spinoff and has dragged down IBM's earnings. The company is now focusing on the hybrid-cloud market to boost growth and better compete with rivals like Amazon.com Inc and Microsoft Corp.

title: The Strategy to Build Secure Multi-cloud Networking
summary: This article discusses the strategy for building secure multi-cloud networking, emphasizing that successful multi-cloud adoption requires a network architecture that facilitates application distribution while maintaining security, configuration policies, and performance. It highlights the benefits of a multi-cloud approach, such as service choice, reduced vendor lock-in, low latency, and improved disaster recovery, while also addressing common challenges like complex management and inconsistent security policies. The paper proposes an application-aware, cloud-ready network architecture with software-defined networking as a core component to achieve efficient and secure multi-cloud environments.

title: Microsoft’s 2021 Diversity & Inclusion report: Demonstrating progress and remaining accountable to our commitments
summary: Microsoft's Chief Diversity Officer, Lindsay-Rae McIntyre, shares the company's 2021 Diversity & Inclusion report, highlighting progress in workforce representation across various groups. The report emphasizes measurement and data, along with employee experiences, showcasing increases in representation for women, Black and African American, Hispanic and Latinx, and Asian employees, as well as those self-identifying with a disability. It also details advancements at leadership levels and Microsoft's commitment to its Racial Equity Initiative goals.

title: PayPal in $45 bln bid for Pinterest -sources
summary: PayPal Holdings Inc is reportedly offering to acquire digital pinboard site Pinterest Inc for $45 billion, mostly in stock, which would be the largest acquisition of a social media company. The potential deal aims to capitalize on the growing social commerce trend and diversify PayPal's income with advertising revenue. While no deal is certain, the proposed offer represents a 26% premium to Pinterest's recent closing price.

title: GEP doubles global partner network of consulting and technology firms
summary: GEP, a supply chain software and consulting firm, has expanded its Partner United program by 114% since January 2021, doubling its global network of consulting and technology firms. This growth is driven by increasing client demand for digitally optimized supply chains, with new partners like Optis Consulting, Synergy Partners, Stratesys, Dun & Bradstreet, Pagero, and TealBook joining the initiative. The program aims to leverage diverse industry expertise and regional specializations to deliver immediate results to clients facing global supply chain challenges.

title: Aruba Launches Network Switch Armed with Pensando Programmable Chip
summary: Aruba has partnered with silicon startup Pensando to launch the CX 10000 Series network switch, integrating Pensando's Elba DPU to provide various network services as distributed functions. This new switch aims to help enterprises manage east-west traffic more efficiently and cost-effectively, bringing hyperscaler networking capabilities to their own data centers. It promises significant improvements in performance and scalability by offloading tasks typically handled by separate appliances directly into the network fabric.

title: NICE Nexidia AI Analytics Review: Flexible Service To Suit You
summary: The NICE Nexidia AI Analytics platform offers a comprehensive suite of tools for businesses to analyze customer interactions across all channels. It helps companies understand customer sentiment, predict churn, improve call quality, and ensure compliance through features like speech and text analytics, real-time monitoring, and audio discovery. The service is flexible and modular, allowing businesses to tailor analytics to their specific needs, ultimately improving customer loyalty and business decision-making.

title: NVIDIA Introduces the Next Generation in Cloud Gaming
summary: NVIDIA has announced its next-generation cloud gaming platform, GeForce NOW, which will offer GeForce RTX 3080-class gaming performance through a new high-performance membership tier. This tier leverages NVIDIA's SuperPOD architecture, providing significant graphical horsepower and enabling high resolutions, fast frame rates, and low latency across various devices. The service provides access to over 1,100 games, including many popular free-to-play and upcoming titles with RTX ON.

title: Microsoft cloud agreement aims to boost NZ health service equity – New Zealand News Centre
summary: Microsoft New Zealand has signed a three-year cloud services agreement with the Accident Compensation Corporation (ACC) to migrate its New Zealand operations to Azure. This agreement aims to enhance ACC's data utilization for better healthcare pathways and more equitable health outcomes across the country. It also positions ACC to leverage Microsoft's forthcoming hyperscale datacenter region in New Zealand for secure data storage and scalable capacity.

title: Kickstart your internal communications strategy with these best practices
summary: This article provides a comprehensive guide to developing an effective internal communications strategy, highlighting its increased importance in a remote and hybrid work environment. It outlines seven key steps, from assessing current strategies and setting goals to segmenting audiences and identifying communication tools, and further details best practices for engaging employees and building a strong company culture. The piece emphasizes the necessity of measuring progress and continually optimizing internal communication efforts to improve employee engagement, productivity, and retention.

title: Workday Named a Leader in the 2021 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Cloud HCM Suites for 1,000+ Employee Enterprises
summary: Workday has been recognized as a Leader in the 2021 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Cloud HCM Suites for 1,000+ Employee Enterprises for the sixth consecutive year, achieving the highest position overall for its ability to execute. This recognition highlights Workday's commitment to helping organizations navigate challenges like the “Great Resignation” by focusing on skills transformation and enhancing the employee experience through solutions like Workday Skills Cloud, Peakon, and Workday Everywhere. The company continues to invest in scaling its offerings to support complex global organizations, maintaining a high customer satisfaction score of 97%.

title: Diversification away from Taiwan chipmakers is necessary
summary: The article discusses the global reliance on Taiwan's chipmakers, particularly TSMC, amidst a worldwide chip shortage. It highlights efforts by South Korea, China, and the U.S. (Intel, GlobalFoundries) to diversify semiconductor production, acknowledging the difficulties due to high capital investment and technological complexity. The author concludes that while diversification is necessary, it will be a challenging and time-consuming process given Taiwan's established and highly specialized chipmaking ecosystem.

title: Wells Fargo has a new virtual assistant in the works named Fargo
summary: Wells Fargo is developing a new virtual assistant named Fargo to enhance its digital banking experience and boost customer engagement. The assistant, expected to launch in 2022, will enable users to pay bills, send money, and receive budgeting advice, aiming to convert more retail customers to digital platforms. This initiative is part of CEO Charles Scharf's broader technology overhaul to update the bank's aging systems and improve its digital offerings, particularly given its historical lag in digital adoption compared to rivals.

title: PayPal says it is currently not pursuing Pinterest acquisition
summary: PayPal has announced it is not currently pursuing an acquisition of Pinterest, following media reports last week of a potential $45 billion deal. This news caused Pinterest's share price to drop over 12%, though analysts suggest Pinterest might still attract other bidders due to its valuation and recent share decline. The potential deal had faced skepticism from investors and analysts, who highlighted significant integration risks and PayPal's lack of experience in user engagement platforms.

title: Mindtree Launches Industry-Specific IoT Solutions Built on ServiceNow Connected Operations
summary: Mindtree has launched new industry-specific IoT solutions leveraging ServiceNow Connected Operations. These solutions are designed to enhance operational efficiency and service management across various sectors. The article highlights the strategic collaboration between Mindtree and ServiceNow to deliver advanced IoT capabilities.

title: Navitas Semiconductor Goes Public With $1.7B Valuation
summary: Navitas Semiconductor went public on October 20 under the symbol "NVTS" with a market value of roughly $2 billion, having completed a reverse merger with Live Oak Acquisition Corp. II. The company, which develops gallium nitride semiconductors, expects $27 million in revenue for 2021 and anticipates its revenue to more than double next year with an influx of $320 million from going public, allowing expansion into data centers, solar, and electric vehicles. Co-founders Gene Sheridan and Dan Kinzer celebrated the IPO seven years after starting the El Segundo-based company.

title: Silicon Valley Battery Veteran Ronnie Tao Joins Amprius Technologies As Vice President Of Business Development
summary: Amprius Technologies, Inc. announced the appointment of Ronnie Tao as Vice President of Business Development. Tao brings extensive experience from companies like Sony Electronics and Amazon, and will focus on expanding Amprius's market reach for its high-energy density lithium-ion batteries. This strategic hire aims to capitalize on increasing commercial opportunities for their Silicon Nanowire anode battery platform.

title: CEO Says Bank of America is a Technology Company
summary: Bank of America CEO Brian Moynihan stated at Yahoo Finance’s All Markets Summit that he views the bank as a financial technology company due to its extensive digital operations and significant technology investments. The company has seen substantial growth in digital banking users and transactions, incorporating features like Zelle and virtual assistant Erica. Bank of America's commitment to digital innovation has contributed to an 80% stock increase over the past three years.

title: AMD sales rise 54% on strong demand for chips for servers and game consoles
summary: AMD reported strong third-quarter earnings, beating analyst expectations for both revenue and EPS, driven by high demand for its chips in PCs, servers, and game consoles. The company also issued a robust forecast for the fourth quarter, expecting continued growth in server and semi-custom segments amidst ongoing chip shortages. AMD's strategic acquisition of Xilinx is proceeding, aiming to strengthen its position in the data center market.

title: Photoshop’s AI Is Now So Fast That Hovering Over Objects Instantly Creates Perfect Masks
summary: Adobe Photoshop has received a major update that significantly streamlines the masking process using AI-powered technology. Users can now simply hover their mouse over an object to instantly create a mask, and a new "Mask All Objects" feature automatically generates separate masks for every detected object. Additionally, Adobe announced that Photoshop and Illustrator will be available as limited-functionality beta versions on the web for Chrome and Edge browsers, facilitating easier collaboration.

title: AI is refashioning software development
summary: Artificial intelligence is transforming software development by enabling developers to use AI for writing and reviewing code, detecting bugs, and optimizing projects. This shift, referred to as Software 2.0, utilizes neural networks and deep learning to create programs through examples rather than explicit instructions. While AI-powered tools enhance efficiency and democratize coding, they are largely seen as augmenting human developers rather than replacing them, accelerating work and eliminating some tasks while still requiring human oversight.

title: Opinion | Tesla Is Worth $1 Trillion
summary: Tesla Inc. has achieved a market capitalization exceeding $1 trillion, a significant milestone driven recently by a large order from Hertz for 100,000 Model 3 cars. This makes Tesla's valuation higher than the next nine largest automakers combined, demonstrating Elon Musk's success as a market disrupter. Despite this success, the article questions why the company still relies on taxpayer subsidies.

title: Predictions 2022: This Is A Year To Be Bold
summary: Forrester's 2022 Predictions anticipate a year of bold decisions driven by critical business trends such as heightened expectations for digital experiences and the shift to human-centered technology transformations. The article highlights key predictions including consumers viewing the world as "ALL digital," B2B marketers adopting "always on" strategies but missing ROI goals, and accessibility becoming a major CX priority. It also forecasts that one-third of firms shifting to hybrid work models will fail without adapting their processes.

title: Cybersecurity More Important Than Ever as Russia-Linked Hackers Target Tech Companies
summary: Microsoft announced that Russia-linked hackers, responsible for the 2020 SolarWinds hack, have significantly increased their attacks on technology companies this year, targeting 609 companies 22,868 times. These attacks highlight the growing need for enhanced cybersecurity measures and investment. The article also discusses the ProShares Ultra Nasdaq Cybersecurity ETF (UCYB) as an investment vehicle for exposure to the cybersecurity sector.

title: Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ:MSFT) Will not be Taken Private, But it Might go to US$420
summary: Microsoft Corporation continues its strong performance, reporting solid earnings and expanding partnerships. A discounted cash flow (DCF) analysis suggests the company might be undervalued, with an estimated intrinsic value higher than its current trading price, driven by growth in all three business segments and an expanded share buyback program. The article details the methodology and key financial metrics supporting the valuation, emphasizing positive catalysts for future growth.

title: Microsoft brought 1,500 jobs to Atlanta. A wave of tech investments followed.
summary: Microsoft's expansion in Atlanta, bringing 1,500 jobs with its Atlantic Yards office, has spurred further technology investments in the city. The state views Microsoft's presence as a catalyst for attracting other Fortune 500 tech companies, particularly from the West Coast. This move is seen as a significant development for Atlanta's technology sector.

title: Saudi Arabia’s rivalry with Dubai for regional HQs heats up
summary: Saudi Arabia is intensifying its efforts to attract regional headquarters, offering tax breaks and other incentives to 7,000 global firms to establish a presence in Riyadh, directly challenging Dubai's long-held status as the region's business hub. Over 40 multinational companies have already received licenses as part of this initiative, with the kingdom aiming for 480 companies by 2030. This aggressive push is supported by a policy that will prevent Saudi government entities from contracting with foreign companies whose regional headquarters are not located in the kingdom from 2024.

title: Shopify-incubated Ottawa startup Fellow raises US$24-million as meeting-management software sales surge
summary: Fellow Insights Inc., an Ottawa-based meeting management software provider, has secured US$24-million in a venture capital financing round led by Craft Ventures. The company, which was initially incubated by Shopify Inc., develops software to enhance meeting productivity and has seen its customer base triple in the past year, with revenues on track to quadruple. Its growth has accelerated during the pandemic due to the rise in virtual and hybrid meetings.

title: Microsoft named a Leader in 2021 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for CRM Customer Engagement Center
summary: Microsoft has been recognized as a Leader in the 2021 Gartner Magic Quadrant for CRM Customer Engagement Center for the eighth consecutive year, highlighting its continuous investment and authority in service solutions and cloud functionality. The company emphasizes its commitment to delivering innovative features through three pillars: tailoring customer engagements, elevating employee effectiveness, and optimizing service operations. This recognition reinforces Microsoft's role in helping organizations reimagine customer service and drive new revenue streams with Dynamics 365 Customer Service.

title: The 100 Most Influential Irish Americans in Business: W. Connell – T. Corcoran
summary: This article highlights three influential Irish American businessmen: William F. Connell, Chairman & CEO of Connell Limited Partnership; John G. Connors, Vice President at Microsoft Corporation; and Thomas A. Corcoran, President & CEO of Allegheny Teledyne, Inc. It details their career achievements, business acumen, and strong connections to their Irish heritage through family roots and involvement in Irish American organizations like The American Ireland Fund.

title: Goldman Sachs, Harvard team up with Al Gore’s investment firm
summary: Al Gore's investment firm, Generation Investment Management LLP, is partnering with Goldman Sachs Asset Management, Microsoft Climate Innovation Fund, and Harvard Management Co. to launch "Just Climate." This new venture aims to channel capital into companies and projects focused on decarbonizing the economy, with the goal of limiting global warming to 1.5 degrees Celsius. The initiative highlights a shift from traditional ESG investing, which is seen as insufficient to address the urgent climate crisis, towards more direct "climate-led investing."

title: Trimble and Microsoft Partner to Drive Digital Transformation Across Industries
summary: Trimble and Microsoft have announced a strategic partnership to accelerate digital transformation in the construction, agriculture, and transportation industries. Their initial focus will be on building the "Trimble Construction Cloud" powered by Microsoft Azure, aimed at improving productivity, reducing costs, and increasing collaboration in the fragmented construction sector. This collaboration expands their existing relationship, leveraging Microsoft's cloud technologies with Trimble's industry expertise to deliver innovative solutions and support infrastructure investments in 2022.

title: US tech company NetApp to open international headquarters in Cork
summary: US-based technology company NetApp is establishing its international headquarters in Cork, Ireland, aiming to create up to 500 jobs by 2025. This expansion is part of NetApp's strategy to grow its business and international presence, capitalizing on Ireland's strong ecosystem for tech companies and skilled graduates. The new office will support its global operations outside the US, aligning with the accelerated digital transformation trends observed during the Covid-19 pandemic.

title: Former GE CEO Jeff Immelt: 'The GE story is a complicated story'
summary: Former General Electric CEO Jeff Immelt has released a new book, "Hot Seat," where he aims to fully explain the "complicated story" of GE's decline during his 16-year tenure. Immelt attributes the company's struggles to external factors like globalization and digitization, as well as multiple crises post-9/11 and the 2008 financial crash that severely impacted GE Capital. He hopes his insights into crisis leadership will be valuable to other leaders, even as others like Bill Gates have described GE's downfall as a "textbook case of mismanagement."

title: bp and Infosys to develop ‘Energy as a Service’ solution for campuses and cities | BP India news | bp India - Home
summary: BP and Infosys are collaborating to develop and pilot an 'Energy as a Service' (EaaS) solution aimed at improving energy efficiency and achieving decarbonization goals for businesses. They plan to co-develop a digital platform that uses AI to optimize energy supply and demand, starting with a pilot at the Infosys Pune Development Center. This initiative seeks to integrate solar energy, manage power for various uses including EV charging, and eventually roll out across other campuses and clients in India.

title: Commvault Metallic launches backup security dashboard
summary: Commvault Metallic has launched Metallic Security IQ, a new dashboard designed to provide visibility into potential security vulnerabilities in Metallic backup environments. The tool calculates a security posture score and gamifies security to encourage IT admins to address weaknesses, directly benefiting both end customers and managed service providers (MSPs) in protecting against cyberattacks like ransomware. This initiative reflects a growing trend among backup vendors to integrate security with data protection.

title: Dual Interface Payment Card Market Size Report, 2022-2030
summary: The global dual interface payment card market reached USD 8,026.4 million in 2023 and is projected to grow at a CAGR of 16.7% from 2024 to 2030, driven by advancements in payment card chips, integration of NFC and RFID, and increasing demand for contactless payments. Key factors include consumer preference for fast and secure transactions, the COVID-19 pandemic's impact on contactless adoption, and rising demand in the banking sector for biometric-integrated cards. The market also faces challenges such as security concerns and the cost of hardware upgrades, with plastic and retail segments holding significant shares.

title: Invesco ESG NASDAQ 100 ETF
summary: This page provides a comprehensive guide to the Invesco ESG NASDAQ 100 ETF (QQMG), detailing its profile, price, dividend, valuation, expense ratio, holdings, and performance metrics. It includes vital information like its inception date, index tracked, assets under management, and comparisons to alternative ETFs. The report also highlights the ETF's ESG themes and scores, geographical exposure, sector allocation, and volatility analysis.

title: Microsoft unseats Apple as most valuable company
summary: Microsoft has surpassed Apple to become the world's most valuable company following Apple's rare quarterly sales miss due to chip shortages and supply chain issues. Microsoft currently holds a market capitalization of approximately $2.48 trillion, slightly exceeding Apple's $2.47 trillion. This shift comes after Apple reported fourth-quarter sales below Wall Street's projections, while Microsoft's first-quarter revenue significantly beat expectations, driven by strong growth in its Intelligent Cloud segment.

title: Fintech Cybersecurity: A Plan for Innovation with Risk Mitigation
summary: The fintech industry's rapid adoption of new technologies, driven by AI and blockchain, is projected to reach $190 billion by 2026. However, this fast-paced innovation often overlooks critical cybersecurity measures, leaving fintech organizations vulnerable to cyberattacks. The article emphasizes the need for a balanced approach to growth and foundational cybersecurity, advocating for tailored programs and incident response plans to mitigate risks and ensure long-term viability.

title: HealthStream Reinvents Headquarters During COVID-19
summary: HealthStream, a healthcare software developer, redesigned its 67,000 square foot Nashville headquarters during the COVID-19 pandemic to support a hybrid and remote work environment. The company, which already had a remote-friendly culture, equipped its new three-floor office with 71 conference rooms, many featuring video conferencing, and adopted Microsoft Teams with Crestron Flex Mercury devices for seamless communication. This strategic renovation allowed employees to continue working productively from home or the office, ensuring flexibility for the future.

title: Move over Apple, Microsoft now the world’s most valuable company
summary: Microsoft Corp. surpassed Apple Inc. to become the world's most valuable public company after Apple's shares fell due to a $6 billion sales hit from global supply chain issues. Microsoft's stock has surged over 45% this year driven by cloud-based services demand, while Apple, despite robust share buybacks, saw its market capitalization slip below Microsoft's. Both companies face ongoing supply chain challenges, though Microsoft anticipates a strong end to the year for its cloud business.

title: Intel CEO Pat Gelsinger’s “insane” plan to restore the company’s glory days
summary: Intel CEO Pat Gelsinger is implementing an "insane" and ambitious plan to regain the company's market leadership. This involves massive capital expenditures between $25 billion and $28 billion annually, along with $15 billion in R&D, to improve technology and capacity, especially in foundry business. The strategy aims for performance parity by 2024 and industry leadership by 2025, a bold move given Intel's recent struggles against competitors like Apple and ARM-based chips.

title: How Artificial Intelligence is Fueling the Energy Transition
summary: This article discusses how Artificial Intelligence (AI) is crucial for the energy transition to achieve net-zero emissions by 2050 while meeting increasing energy demands. It highlights AI's role in improving efficiency across traditional oil and gas operations and developing new clean energy sources. Companies like Shell are leveraging AI to reduce emissions, cut costs, and enhance safety through predictive maintenance, optimized operations, and development of low-carbon solutions.

title: What could disrupt Amazon?
summary: This article explores potential disruptors for Amazon, analyzing several scenarios ranging from government intervention and environmental policies to technological advancements and cultural shifts. Author David Moschella, a senior IT and Innovation Foundation Fellow, outlines seven key scenarios, emphasizing AWS's critical role and the differences between Amazon and rivals like Microsoft. The piece highlights how traditional tech dominance patterns are evolving, prompting a wider consideration of disruption sources.

title: SEGA and Microsoft to Explore Strategic Alliance to create New Strategic Titles for SEGA and establish a Next-Generation Development Environment｜SEGA CORPORATION
summary: SEGA Corporation and Microsoft Corporation have agreed in principle to a strategic alliance to develop large-scale, global games in a next-generation development environment built on Microsoft’s Azure cloud platform. This alliance is crucial for SEGA's "Super Game" initiative, focusing on global, online, community, and IP utilization. The collaboration aims to optimize development processes and enhance gaming experiences through advanced cloud technologies.

title: Industry Report: Technology’s primary role in 2022 is to increase revenue
summary: A report by WTM London and Travel Forward indicates that industry professionals view technology's main role in 2022 as increasing revenue, with cost reduction being the third most important factor. The research, based on a survey of nearly 700 senior executives, also highlights a preference for technology to help find new clients and source markets over retaining existing customers. This suggests an underlying optimism in the industry for market growth and an expanded customer base in the coming year.

title: Facebook to shut down facial recognition system, delete face prints of 1 billion users
summary: Facebook has announced it will shut down its facial recognition system and delete the face prints of over a billion users due to growing concerns about the technology's misuse and increasing regulatory scrutiny. This move, described as one of the largest shifts in facial recognition use, comes amidst a crisis for Facebook (now Meta) and follows years of criticism regarding privacy and the ethics of such technology. While the company stated this specific broad identification method would cease, it did not rule out using facial recognition for narrower authentication purposes in future products, particularly for on-device applications.

title: Tesla Surges to Lift Markets Into New Record Close
summary: Tesla Inc. has surpassed a $1 trillion market value, becoming the most valuable car company, driven by a large order from Hertz and its plan to open its supercharging network to other EV brands. This surge has positively impacted the broader market, with the S&P 500 reaching new highs, and boosting the consumer discretionary sector. The American Century Focused Dynamic Growth ETF (FDG) holds Tesla among its top investments, benefiting from the company's strong performance.

title: Healthcare’s AI Future - In Conversation with Andrew Ng and Fei-Fei Li
summary: This article summarizes a fireside chat between AI experts Andrew Ng and Fei-Fei Li concerning the future of AI in healthcare. It covers four key takeaways: barriers to AI adoption, significant unsolved healthcare problems beyond diagnostics, the importance of empathy and collaboration between technical and non-technical professionals, and strategies for avoiding the perpetuation of bias in AI systems. The experts emphasize the need for human-centered AI that addresses operational issues and incorporates ethical considerations from the outset.

title: Microsoft Cloud at Ignite 2021: Metaverse, AI and hyperconnectivity in a hybrid world
summary: Microsoft unveiled over 90 new services and updates at Ignite 2021, focusing on the metaverse, AI breakthroughs, and building a trust fabric. Key announcements include Dynamics 365 Connected Spaces and Mesh for Microsoft Teams to power metaverse experiences, and the Azure OpenAI Service for enterprise-grade AI. The company emphasizes enabling hybrid work, hyperconnected businesses, and end-to-end security through these innovations.

title: Microsoft reveals its metaverse ambitions by presenting virtual platform Mesh
summary: Microsoft unveiled its plans to integrate metaverse capabilities into its Teams platform with the launch of Mesh. This new platform will enable users to create 3D avatars for virtual meetings and immersive experiences, without requiring VR headsets. Microsoft also aims to bring its metaverse ambitions to gaming, seeing titles like Halo and Minecraft as foundational to this vision.

title: VM-Series Virtual Firewalls Integrate with Azure Gateway Load Balancer
summary: Palo Alto Networks has integrated its VM-Series virtual firewalls with Microsoft Azure Gateway Load Balancer, enhancing Azure's native network security with next-generation threat protection. This integration, now in beta, provides improved performance, scalability, full visibility of traffic sources, and supports zone-based policies for internet ingress traffic. It aims to secure applications and data in Azure by preventing various threats and enabling easier management of security policies.

title: Iron Mountain’s Hollywood Treasures
summary: Iron Mountain Entertainment Services' Hollywood facility safeguards significant assets from theatrical and TV production history, including iconic props and celebrity documents. The company offers secure physical storage in an earthquake-resistant building, along with digital asset management, digitization, and media services, focusing on preserving older formats and leveraging cloud security for remote access. This comprehensive approach ensures the secure storage and accessibility of invaluable media and entertainment archives.

title: Johnson & Johnson advances global health and avoids supply chain disruptions - Source
summary: Johnson & Johnson leverages its collaboration with Microsoft to implement digital manufacturing transformation, including Azure, AI, and IoT, to enhance its global supply chain efficiency and resilience. By shifting to a pull supply chain and using smart manufacturing, J&J can ensure products are delivered precisely when needed, reduce errors, and mitigate disruptions. The company has seen improved quality output, a reduction in "field actions," and moved from 28th to 3rd globally in Gartner's Magic Quadrant for Supply Chain Leaders, driven by its technological advancements.

title: André Christ, CEO of LeanIX: Leveraging corporate experience to bootstrap a startup
summary: André Christ, CEO of LeanIX, discusses his journey from working at DHL to founding his own startup. He highlights how his corporate experience helped him identify a market need for IT landscape transparency and validate his business idea. Christ also shares insights into bootstrapping LeanIX for three years and the challenges and successes of acquiring early enterprise customers.

title: Mesh for Microsoft Teams aims to make collaboration in the ‘metaverse’ personal and fun
summary: Microsoft unveiled Mesh for Microsoft Teams, a new feature combining mixed-reality capabilities with productivity tools to make online collaboration more personal and engaging. This initiative addresses the challenges of remote work by allowing users to join meetings as customized avatars and create immersive virtual spaces, serving as a gateway to the metaverse. The feature aims to enhance team effectiveness and individual engagement by bringing the spontaneity and personal connection of in-person interactions to virtual environments.

title: Big data and analytics to reach $684.12 billion by 2030
summary: The global big data and business analytics market is projected to reach $684.12 billion by 2030, growing at a CAGR of 13.5% from 2021. This growth is driven by the vast amounts of data generated by online and offline trading and the increasing adoption of cloud solutions by SMEs. The banking, financial services, and insurance sector is expected to be the most lucrative segment, with emerging trends like social media and text analytics creating new opportunities.

title: Microsoft and AES Partner to Bring Around-the-Clock Renewable Energy to Data Centers
summary: Microsoft and AES have signed a 15-year agreement to provide around-the-clock renewable energy to Microsoft's data centers in Virginia. This partnership supports Microsoft's goal of achieving 100/100/0 by 2030, meaning 100% of its electricity consumption will be matched by 100% zero-carbon sources, 100% of the time, in all grids, every day. AES will supply the energy from a portfolio of wind, solar, and battery energy storage projects.

title: Microsoft’s GitHub CEO Nat Friedman is stepping down, product chief Thomas Dohmke will replace him
summary: Nat Friedman, CEO of Microsoft's GitHub subsidiary, is stepping down and will be replaced by Thomas Dohmke, GitHub's product chief, effective November 15. Friedman plans to return to his startup roots and will serve as an advisor to both GitHub and Microsoft. This transition comes as GitHub's competitor, GitLab, recently went public with a valuation more than double what Microsoft paid for GitHub in 2018.

title: Microsoft-Sega deal: Don't expect an acquisition soon
summary: Sega announced a "strategic alliance" with Microsoft and Xbox in October 2021, focusing on using Microsoft's Azure cloud platform for large-scale game development. While not an acquisition, given the difficulty for Western companies to acquire Japanese studios, this partnership deepens ties and could lead to more meaningful collaborations, potentially including closer integration for Sega's future games and even exclusivity on Xbox platforms. The deal primarily leverages Microsoft's cloud dominance to help Sega develop "super games" with a focus on community and IP utilization.

title: 10 things Microsoft has learned about successful hybrid work
summary: Microsoft's HR Vice President, Amy Coleman, shared 10 key learnings from their experience managing a hybrid workforce of over 175,000 employees across 74 countries since the pandemic. These insights highlight the importance of a strong culture, employee well-being, effective managers, active listening, and flexible work arrangements. The company also learned about the need to build social capital creatively, foster inclusion, leverage technology, adapt to new talent expectations, and cultivate a growth mindset.

title: AT&T selects Amdocs to support its Business Support Systems evolution to make life easier and enjoyable for customers
summary: AT&T has chosen Amdocs' CES cloud-native platform to support its Business Support Systems evolution (BSSe) program, aimed at modernizing and simplifying technology. This long-term agreement includes next-generation cloud operations for BSSe, launching on Microsoft Azure and initially focusing on AT&T's consumer business units, including mobility with 5G, fixed wireless, broadband, and IoT. The initiative seeks to increase speed-to-market, improve customer experiences, and achieve long-term cost-effectiveness.

title: Monthly Market Wrap - October 2021
summary: The October 2021 market wrap highlights a month of economic observations including rising inflation, the Federal Reserve's anticipated tapering, and varied performance across domestic and international equities. It also covers positive trends in alternative investments and the increasing integration of ESG factors into investment strategies. The report details specific market indices and economic indicators, providing a comprehensive overview of the financial landscape during the month.

title: Investing in Mark Zuckerberg’s vision of the Metaverse with an ETF
summary: This article discusses investing in Mark Zuckerberg's vision of the Metaverse following Facebook's rebranding to Meta. It explains what the Metaverse is, how investors can gain exposure through companies involved in its creation like Roblox and Unity Software, and highlights the Roundhill Ball Metaverse ETF (NYSE:META) which tracks a basket of such stocks. The article also provides information on thematic ETFs and the fund manager, Roundhill Investments.

title: Israeli firm Beamr awarded Emmy for video compression tech
summary: The Israeli company Beamr received an Emmy in the Technology & Engineering category from the National Academy of Television Arts and Sciences for its patented video compression technology. This technology reduces video file sizes while maintaining high quality, benefiting streaming services and broadcasters. Beamr's solution uses a quality measure called BQM to adjust bitrate automatically, saving bandwidth and improving efficiency for major clients like Netflix and Microsoft.

title: Update: Tencent Unveils Three Computer Chips of Its Own Design
summary: Tencent Holdings Ltd., a leading Chinese software firm, has announced the development of three proprietary computer chips: an AI computing chip (Zixiao), a video processor (Canghai), and a network interface controller (Xuanling). This move signals Tencent's increased entry into the hardware business, following other Chinese tech giants like Alibaba and Huawei, and aims to reduce costs and gain a competitive edge amidst global chip shortages and policy support for domestic chip development. While these chips are currently less complex than general-purpose chips developed by rivals, Tencent plans long-term investment in this area.

title: Google acquires $1B stake in CME Group as companies ink 10-year cloud deal
summary: CME Group Inc., a major operator of financial exchanges, has partnered with Google LLC for a 10-year cloud deal to migrate its technology infrastructure to Google Cloud. As part of this agreement, Google made a significant investment, acquiring $1 billion worth of CME Group stock. This partnership aims to scale CME Group's IT infrastructure, streamline operations, and enhance various technology capabilities, including risk mitigation tools and data analytics services for clients.

title: Kyndryl Debuts: 10 Things To Know On The IBM Spin-Off
summary: Kyndryl, the spun-off managed infrastructure services business from IBM, has debuted as an independent company. Despite being the world's largest IT infrastructure services provider with 90,000 employees, Kyndryl faces challenges including three years of revenue decline and net losses, with analysts predicting positive revenue growth not before 2025. The company will focus on six global managed services practices, a strong leadership team, and a robust board of directors, while maintaining a significant commercial relationship with IBM.

title: What’s Changed: 2021 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Data Quality Solutions
summary: This article analyzes Gartner's 2021 Magic Quadrant for Data Quality Solutions, highlighting the evolving landscape of data quality management. It discusses the inclusion and exclusion of vendors, the shift towards augmented data quality, and the increasing convergence with other data software segments. Key leaders identified are Informatica, SAP, and IBM, with other vendors like Ataccama, Experian, and Talend also making significant moves.

title: Kyndryl CTO Antoine Shagoury: IP ‘War Chest’ Part Of Competitive Advantage
summary: Kyndryl CTO Antoine Shagoury discusses the company's competitive advantages after spinning off from IBM, highlighting its vast intellectual property, operational expertise, and freedom to partner with other vendors. He also discusses how Kyndryl helps clients with digital transformation, modernization, and automation, leveraging its extensive data insights and experience. Shagoury emphasizes the importance of Kyndryl's ability to demonstrate tangible value to clients rather than just talking about abstract technological solutions.

title: T-Mobile adopts Microsoft Power Platform for fast and powerful low-code development
summary: T-Mobile has embraced Microsoft Power Platform for low-code development, enabling employees across various backgrounds to create solutions that improve business processes and operational insights. These solutions range from managing device promotion approvals to developing apps for store closure and staffing management during COVID-19. The company is actively fostering an internal Power Platform community and plans to establish a Center of Excellence to further promote low-code initiatives and ensure secure, scalable development.

title: How WPP CIO Rachel Higham is simplifying IT and rethinking diversity
summary: WPP's first CIO, Rachel Higham, is spearheading an ambitious initiative to simplify IT operations, consolidate numerous agency technologies, and foster global platforms to enhance business agility. Her strategy includes a strong focus on sustainability, aiming for net-zero carbon emissions by 2025 in operations and 2030 across the supply chain, while also tackling diversity and inclusion within the IT department and among vendor partners. Higham's approach emphasizes serving the broader business transformation and leveraging technology to meet both operational and ethical objectives.

title: Arista Gains Big on Cloud Boom
summary: Arista Networks experienced significant stock gains following strong earnings and boosted guidance, driven by increased capital spending from hyperscalers like Meta and Microsoft. The company also continues to gain market share from competitors like Cisco in both data center, cloud, and campus networking segments, indicating a robust cloud boom across the industry. Other infrastructure vendors like NVIDIA, Amazon Web Services, and Broadcom are also seeing growth.

title: Micron Technology to invest more than US$150 bln globally in manufacturing and R&D until 2030
summary: Micron Technology announced plans to invest over US$150 billion globally by 2030 in leading-edge memory manufacturing and R&D, including potential US fab expansion. This investment aims to meet the increasing demand for memory, essential for computing driven by technologies like 5G and AI. The company, which already has extensive global operations, is optimistic about its growth in Malaysia and expects strong revenue and profit margins in 2022.

title: New Working Group for the Software-Defined Vehicle
summary: The Eclipse Foundation, in collaboration with industry leaders like Bosch and Microsoft, has announced an open invitation to technology leaders to participate in a new working group focused on the Software-Defined Vehicle. The goal is to create a vendor-agnostic, open-source ecosystem to foster advancements in automotive software development. EPAM, through its expertise in embedded engineering and digital orchestration, is actively supporting this initiative.

title: What’s Changed: 2021 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Content Services Platforms
summary: Gartner has released its 2021 Magic Quadrant for Content Services Platforms (CSPs), evaluating 18 vendors in a mature market marked by a rapid shift towards cloud-based PaaS/SaaS solutions. The report identifies Microsoft, Hyland, Box, and OpenText as leaders, while classifying the remaining vendors as Niche Players or Visionaries, with no Challengers named this year. Key changes include the addition of Fabasoft, d.velop, and Intalio, and the increased importance of integration with existing business application ecosystems.

title: Do you use your work email for personal transactions?
summary: A study by SailPoint Technologies revealed that over half of workers use their corporate emails for personal use, significantly increasing the risk of phishing and cyber attacks. Gen Z and Millennials are particularly prone to using work emails for social media logins and online shopping. The article emphasizes the critical need for proper employee education and training to mitigate these security risks, as many employees do not know how to respond to suspicious activities.

title: Google invests $1bn into Chicago Mercantile Exchange as part of cloud migration deal
summary: Google Cloud has signed a 10-year deal with CME Group to migrate all of CME's infrastructure and markets to the cloud starting in early 2022. As part of this agreement, Google has also made a $1 billion equity investment in CME Group. The partnership aims to enhance CME's services, introduce new products, and accelerate technological innovation in capital markets while strengthening Google Cloud's position in the financial services sector.

title: ‘Business needs a noble purpose and a human-centric approach — these core principles revived Best Buy’
summary: Hubert Joly, former CEO of Best Buy, discusses how a human-centric approach and noble purpose revived the company, leading its share price to rise 11-fold. He emphasizes that putting people at the center and embracing all stakeholders is crucial for businesses today, especially in navigating challenges like the pandemic and climate change. Joly argues that the "Milton Friedman doctrine" of profit-first is outdated and highlights companies like Microsoft, Ralph Lauren, and Unilever as examples of successful human-centric models.

title: 112 Hardware Heroes Changing Quantum Tech — Part 1: Specialists 1–14
summary: This article highlights the crucial "Hardware Heroes" in the quantum technology sector, focusing on the specialized engineers and researchers who build and test quantum hardware. It features the first 14 individuals in a series of 112 profiles, shedding light on their expertise in various quantum approaches like superconducting, trapped ions, and cold atoms, and their contributions to companies such as Alice & Bob, Aliro, and ColdQuanta. The piece emphasizes that while founders and CEOs receive much credit, the foundational work is done by these specialists in the "trenches."

title: EXPLAINED: What is Metaverse and Why Facebook/ Meta Thinks it's the Future of Internet
summary: This article explains the concept of the metaverse, why Facebook (now Meta) views it as the future of the internet, and what its potential applications are. It details how the metaverse would work, from virtual interactions and business opportunities to the technologies being developed to build it, while also touching on data privacy concerns.

title: AMD shares close up 10% after company wins Meta partnership, announces new chips
summary: AMD shares surged 10% after the company announced a partnership with Meta (formerly Facebook) as a chip customer and unveiled a new range of chips at its Accelerated Data Center Premiere event. This move strengthens AMD's position against competitors like Intel, as the company continues to gain market share with its data center chip sales experiencing significant growth. Additional details about the Meta partnership are expected to be revealed later in the week at the Open Compute Project summit.

title: Poll Finds Gamers Are Most Interested in EA, Rockstar of Major Publishers
summary: A Morning Consult poll found that Electronic Arts (EA) and Rockstar Games are the top publishers capturing gamers' interest, with 64% and 61% of avid gamers interested, respectively. Despite controversies, Ubisoft and Activision also ranked highly. CD Projekt Red, however, ranked near the bottom, likely due to issues with its Cyberpunk 2077 launch.

title: What’s Changed: 2021 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Network Firewalls
summary: Gartner has released its 2021 Magic Quadrant for Network Firewalls, analyzing 19 providers based on their ability to execute and completeness of vision. The report highlights the evolution of network firewalls into comprehensive platforms, with a growing trend towards virtual appliances, cloud-native firewalls, and Firewall as a Service (FWaaS). Key changes include the addition and removal of several vendors, with Palo Alto Networks, Fortinet, and Check Point Software Technologies recognized as leaders in the current market.

title: CMO of the Week: Campbell Soup Company’s Linda Lee
summary: Linda Lee, CMO of Meals and Beverages at Campbell Soup Company, discusses the company's recent initiatives, including the first redesign of its iconic soup can in over 50 years and partnerships with artists and music labels. She also details how Campbell's adapted its marketing strategy and media mix during the pandemic, focusing on digital engagement, entertainment, and diversity & inclusion efforts.

title: Google’s parent Alphabet breaches $2 trillion in market value
summary: Google's parent company, Alphabet Inc., reached a $2 trillion market valuation for the first time, driven by strong growth in digital advertising and its cloud business. This puts Alphabet in an exclusive club with Apple Inc. and Microsoft Corp., with analysts remaining optimistic about its future growth due to a cheaper valuation and increasing cloud adoption.

title: OpenText to acquire Zix in $860 million deal meant to bolster Microsoft relationship
summary: OpenText has announced an agreement to acquire Texas-based Zix for $860 million USD, including debt. This acquisition aims to create a "powerhouse SMB platform" for data protection, threat management, and compliance solutions by integrating Zix's offerings with OpenText's previous acquisitions, Carbonite and Webroot, and to deepen its relationship with Microsoft. The deal is expected to expand OpenText's cloud revenues, adjusted EBITDA, and cash flows.

title: Microsoft is a 5-time Leader in the Gartner Magic Quadrant for Access Management
summary: Microsoft has been recognized as a Leader for the fifth time in the Gartner Magic Quadrant for Access Management for its Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) product. The company also placed furthest right on the "Completeness of Vision" axis, attributing this success to customer feedback. Microsoft highlights three key trends shaping its product vision: deeper integration of access control for Zero Trust, multi-cloud security and governance, and building a new trust fabric for decentralized computing and digital ecosystems.

title: Zscaler Moves Into UCaaS Monitoring
summary: Zscaler has expanded its cloud security product, Zscaler Digital Experience (ZDX), to include monitoring for UCaaS services like Zoom and Microsoft Teams. This move addresses the challenge of monitoring collaboration services in hybrid work environments, providing IT teams with a single pane of glass for end-to-end application performance. ZDX leverages Zscaler's Zero Trust Exchange to collect and analyze telemetry data, enabling proactive troubleshooting and bridging the gap between security and networking.

title: Microsoft Teams device news, November 2021
summary: This article provides an update on the latest Microsoft Teams device news as of November 2021, covering new features for Teams Rooms and Panels, device management improvements, and SIP Gateway general availability. It also highlights various partnerships and product releases from companies like Bose, Crestron, EPOS, HP, Jabra, Logitech, Poly, Sennheiser, and Yealink, showcasing advancements in hardware for hybrid work environments.

title: Google-owner Alphabet breaches $2 trillion market cap, joins Apple and Microsoft
summary: Google's parent company, Alphabet Inc., reached a $2 trillion market capitalization for the first time, driven by increased digital ad spending and growth in its cloud business. This achievement places Alphabet alongside Apple and Microsoft in the exclusive $2 trillion club. The company reported a record third quarter in 2021 with $65.1 billion in earnings.

title: HP is Using HoloLens to Help Customers Remotely Repair Industrial Printers
summary: HP has launched its 'xRServices' program, equipping industrial printer customers with HoloLens 2 headsets to enable immersive remote support for repairs, training, and troubleshooting. This initiative allows even untrained individuals to fix complex printer issues with live AR-guided instructions from specialists. The program is currently in beta, leveraging AR technology to enhance HP's existing business by providing innovative customer service and training solutions.

title: Readers' Choice 2021
summary: Canadian Lawyer's seventh annual Readers' Choice awards highlights top vendors and service providers in the legal sector, as chosen by its readership. The article showcases how legal professionals are adapting to challenges like the pandemic through increased use of alternative dispute resolution, litigation loans for clients, advanced translation services, and specialized legal technology for document management and estate administration. It features insights from various industry leaders on the evolving needs and technological advancements driving efficiency in legal practices.

title: 5 Charts on General Electric's Fall From Grace
summary: This article details General Electric's significant decline in value over the past two decades, from once being the most valuable company globally to its current 75th position in the U.S. stock market. It attributes GE's fall to a deterioration of culture, poor capital allocation decisions, and an over-reliance on its financial unit. The article discusses GE's recent decision to split into three companies (aviation, healthcare, and energy), a move applauded by analysts and seen as a potential catalyst for closing the persistent price/value gap for the stock.

title: Findings: The 2021 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Access Management
summary: This article highlights key findings from the 2021 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Access Management, evaluating 12 vendors based on their ability to establish, enforce, and manage runtime access controls. Okta, Microsoft, Ping Identity, Auth0, ForgeRock, and OneLogin were identified as leaders or strong contenders. The report details each vendor's strengths, such as product capabilities, innovation, customer experience, and areas for improvement, offering insights into the competitive landscape of the access management market.

title: Microsoft updates its Xbox Game Pass for PC store, allowing users to mod games and choose install folder
summary: Microsoft has announced significant updates to the Xbox Game Pass for PC. These updates will allow users to access local game files for modding and choose custom installation folders, addressing long-standing player complaints. The company aims to provide more customization options for PC gamers on the Xbox app and also plans to improve the experience of finding and downloading upcoming titles.

title: Pegasystems collaborates with Google Cloud to improve healthcare solutions
summary: Pegasystems has partnered with Google Cloud to enhance healthcare experiences by combining Google Cloud’s Healthcare Data Engine with Pega’s intelligent healthcare solutions. This collaboration addresses challenges posed by siloed healthcare systems and the explosion of digital data, enabling better data insights and personalization. The integration aims to facilitate optimized, data-based conversations between consumers and health organizations, leading to improved real-time decisions, patient views, and overall health outcomes.
