title: CVS Health and Microsoft announce new strategic alliance to reimagine personalized care and accelerate digital transformation
summary: CVS Health and Microsoft Corp. announced a new strategic alliance to develop innovative solutions for personalized health care and accelerate digital transformation. This collaboration aims to enhance customer experience, empower over 300,000 CVS Health employees with better tools, and improve operational efficiency across the company, utilizing Microsoft's Azure cloud and AI capabilities. The partnership will focus on data-driven customer experiences, enabling frontline workers, digitalizing operations, and expanding cloud services for CVS Health.

title: Microsoft and CVS Health Partner to Accelerate Personalized Care Experience
summary: CVS Health and Microsoft have announced a new strategic alliance to revolutionize personalized care and accelerate digital transformation. This collaboration aims to leverage data and advanced technologies like Azure and Machine Learning to enhance customer experience, empower over 300,000 CVS Health employees, and improve care access and health outcomes for more than 100 million people. Key initiatives include enabling frontline workers, digitalizing operations, expanding cloud services, and exploring innovative solutions using Microsoft HoloLens and Azure AI.

title: Adopt a data-centric approach to cyber security
summary: This article emphasizes the need for organizations to shift from traditional perimeter-based security to a data-centric approach for cybersecurity. It highlights the importance of discovering and classifying data, implementing a layered security framework, and balancing security with usability. The article also discusses the advantages of cloud-native architectures and emerging AI-based tools for enhancing data protection against evolving cyber threats.

title: U.S. FTC sues to block Nvidia deal to buy Arm
summary: The U.S. Federal Trade Commission (FTC) has sued to block Nvidia Corp's more than $80 billion acquisition of British chip technology provider Arm, citing concerns that the deal would give Nvidia undue control over crucial computing technology and designs. This move complicates an already challenging regulatory path for the acquisition, which has faced opposition from the chip industry and scrutiny from British and European Union regulators. The FTC argues the merger would harm competition, reduce innovation, and lead to higher prices by giving Nvidia the ability and incentive to undermine competitors who rely on Arm's technology.

title: Market Expert: Fall For Quality, Not Just Tech
summary: An article discussing the importance of balancing tech investments with high-quality stocks. It highlights Mark Mahaney's "dislocated high-quality" (DHQ) investment tenet and introduces the FlexShares US Quality Low Volatility Index Fund (QLV) as a suitable option for investors seeking quality and reduced volatility.

title: Can Apple Take Down the World’s Most Notorious Spyware Company?
summary: Apple Inc. has filed a lawsuit against NSO Group Technologies and Q Cyber Technologies, the creators of the Pegasus spyware, which has been used to hack iPhones of journalists, human rights defenders, and government officials worldwide. The article details the widespread use and harmful impact of Pegasus, the background of previous legal actions against NSO Group, and analyzes Apple's legal strategy, highlighting its aggressive stance in protecting user security. The outcome of the lawsuit could significantly impact the future of malicious spyware and state-sponsored hacking.

title: Deloitte buys Oracle Cloud specialist BIAS Corporation
summary: Deloitte US has acquired BIAS Corporation, an IT consultancy specializing in Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI), to enhance its cloud migration capabilities. BIAS, founded in 2000, has over 350 employees and was recognized as an Oracle Global and North American Partner of the Year. This acquisition addresses the increasing demand for cloud services and follows Deloitte's fiscal year 2021 revenue growth to over $50 billion.

title: Market Expert: Fall For Quality, Not Just Tech
summary: A market expert suggests investors prioritize high-quality stocks over solely focusing on big tech names. Mark Mahaney of Evercore ISI advocates for investing in "dislocated high-quality" companies with large total addressable markets and strong innovation, rather than just trading tech stocks. The article highlights the FlexShares US Quality Low Volatility Index Fund (QLV) as an example of an ETF that focuses on quality while managing volatility.

title: Nasdaq dives over 2% as tech stocks slide at end of volatile week
summary: Wall Street's major indexes, particularly the Nasdaq, experienced a significant decline as tech stocks slid at the end of a volatile week. This downturn was influenced by mixed jobs data, uncertainty surrounding the Omicron coronavirus variant, and the Federal Reserve's policy tightening signals. Major tech companies such as Apple, Meta Platforms, Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft, Nvidia, and Tesla all saw their shares fall, contributing to the broader market dip.

title: Moody’s upgrades VPBank’s rating to Ba3
summary: Moody's Investors Service has upgraded Việt Nam Prosperity Bank (VPBank)'s foreign currency deposits from B1 to Ba3, matching the country's rating with a positive outlook. This upgrade follows VPBank's sale of a 49% stake in FE Credit, which improved its capital adequacy ratio and overall financial profile. Moody's also highlighted VPBank's strong business results despite the pandemic and expects continued stability in asset quality and profitability.

title: El ranking de las 100 empresas con mejor reputación de la Argentina
summary: Mercado Libre, Arcor, and Toyota lead the ranking of the 100 most reputable companies in Argentina, according to the Merco 2021 study. Technology, food, cosmetics, and automotive sectors are highlighted, with the top three companies maintaining their positions from the previous year. The study, which surveyed 15,265 individuals, also reveals new entries and significant shifts in reputation for various companies and sectors, emphasizing the resilience of reputation as a key asset during economic challenges.

title: The metaverse needs aggressive regulation
summary: The author, a pioneer in AR/VR technology, argues for aggressive regulation of the metaverse to prevent large corporations from extensive monitoring and manipulation of users. He emphasizes the need to restrict data collection, regulate real-time marketing tactics, and ensure transparency regarding AI-controlled agents and targeted placements. The article warns that without regulation, the metaverse risks becoming an environment where powerful entities exploit user data and emotions for commercial gain.

title: Micron To Bring 500 Tech Jobs To New Atlanta Design Center In Midtown
summary: Micron Technology will open a new Atlanta Design Center in January, creating up to 500 semiconductor jobs in Midtown. The company cited Atlanta's diverse tech-savvy professional pool and STEM graduates as key reasons for the decision, planning to partner with local universities. This move underscores Atlanta's growing reputation as a hub for high-tech innovation, attracting other major companies like Microsoft and Airbnb.

title: Microsoft Seizes 42 Websites From a Chinese Hacking Group (Published 2021)
summary: Microsoft announced on Monday that it had seized 42 websites from a Chinese hacking group known as Nickel or APT15. The group was allegedly using these websites to install malware for intelligence gathering from government agencies, think tanks, universities, and human rights organizations in 29 countries. Microsoft has been tracking Nickel since 2016 and is redirecting the websites' traffic to secure servers to protect victims and learn more about the group's activities.

title: Rigetti’s Superconducting Quantum Computers Now Available Through Azure Quantum
summary: Rigetti Computing has partnered with Microsoft to make its superconducting quantum computers accessible via Microsoft’s Azure Quantum cloud service. This integration, expected in Q1 2022, will provide Azure Quantum users with access to Rigetti's large-scale quantum systems, enabling hybrid quantum-classical computing for various applications like machine learning and drug discovery. The collaboration aims to advance quantum algorithm development and interoperability within the quantum ecosystem.

title: Mobile Threat Defense | Bringing AI-Powered Endpoint Security To Your Mobile Devices
summary: This article discusses the critical need for robust mobile threat defense (MTD) in enterprise environments, especially with the rise of BYOD policies and distributed workforces. It highlights that traditional Mobile Device Management (MDM) solutions are insufficient against modern threats and advocates for advanced MTD integration with XDR platforms like SentinelOne Singularity Mobile to protect against growing mobile-specific attacks. The piece emphasizes that mobile devices are significant targets for cybercriminals, with a sharp increase in zero-day vulnerabilities targeting mobile platforms.

title: CVS enters digital health partnership with Microsoft
summary: CVS Health is partnering with Microsoft to create innovative digital health solutions and enhance its customer experience. This collaboration will leverage Microsoft Azure for advanced machine learning, automate processes, and utilize tools like Microsoft HoloLens to support customers, employees, and partners. CVS Health aims to become a consumer-centric, integrated health solutions company through a digital-first approach.

title: New Aruba EdgeConnect Microbranch Solution Modernizes the Home/Small Office Experience for Hybrid Workplaces
summary: Aruba, a Hewlett Packard Enterprise company, has introduced its new EdgeConnect Microbranch solution, designed to modernize the home and small office experience for hybrid workplaces. This solution provides remote workers with complete in-office connectivity and security services through a single Wi-Fi access point, without requiring additional hardware or agents. It extends SD-WAN and SASE security frameworks to remote locations, ensuring consistent employee experience and bolstering corporate protections.

title: Wärtsilä partners with Microsoft to strengthen their Edge platform and industrialise Marine IoT
summary: Wärtsilä Voyage has partnered with Microsoft to enhance its end-to-end digital services portfolio, bringing all current and future products onto a common platform. This collaboration aims to accelerate the industrialization of IoT for shipping by leveraging Microsoft Azure IoT Edge, thereby improving deployment, maintenance, and cybersecurity for Wärtsilä's marine technologies. The partnership is expected to enable faster deployment of digital solutions, advance autonomy offerings, and contribute to the industry's decarbonization efforts through streamlined Intelligent Edge technology.

title: 5 Free Resources for Tech Learning Include AWS, Coursera, More
summary: This article highlights five free resources for individuals looking to enhance their tech skills: Amazon Web Services (AWS), Coursera, Microsoft Learn, NPower, and Per Scholas. It advises technologists to have clear goals when choosing a program, distinguishing between learning new skills and securing a new job. The resources offer various learning styles, from self-paced online courses to intensive bootcamps, and some provide industry-recognized credentials.

title: Ameriflight Adopts GE Digital’s Aviation Asset Records to Make Actionable Flight Operations Decisions Based on Historical Data | GE News
summary: GE Digital has announced that Ameriflight, the largest Part 135 cargo airline in the U.S., has adopted its Aviation Asset Records software solution. This cloud-based tool will enable Ameriflight to digitize, index, and archive maintenance records, providing actionable insights through automated dashboards and improving decision-making for flight operations. The collaboration aims to leverage data for enhanced efficiency, continuous improvement, and sustainable operations in the face of industry challenges.

title: Microsoft's Joy Chik wants to make passwords obsolete
summary: Joy Chik, Corporate Vice President at Microsoft, is leading an initiative to eliminate passwords for Microsoft's cloud services, aiming to reinvent security. Having started her career at Microsoft as an intern with no prior work experience, Chik has climbed the ranks over 23 years to head the company's identity division. Her daily routine includes early morning workouts, global meetings, strategy discussions, and mentoring, reflecting a dedicated approach to a demanding role.

title: Major Outage Strikes Amazon Web Services ; Netflix, Venmo, Instacart Among Many Affected Sites
summary: A major Amazon Web Services (AWS) outage on December 7, 2021, disrupted numerous popular sites and services, including Netflix, Venmo, and Instacart, and even affected Amazon's own delivery operations. The six-hour disruption, primarily in the eastern U.S., highlighted the growing reliance on centralized cloud services and the cascading impact when they fail, leaving customers and students without access to essential online platforms. Experts noted that such outages are becoming more common due to the centralization and automation of the internet, contrasting with its original design for decentralization.

title: U.S. settles with Microsoft over immigration-related discrimination claims
summary: The U.S. Justice Department has settled with Microsoft Corp over allegations of discriminating against non-U.S. citizens in its hiring process. Microsoft had asked job applicants for unnecessary immigration documents to prove work eligibility without sponsorship. As part of the settlement, Microsoft will revise its hiring procedures to comply with U.S. law.

title: Zscaler Extends its Proven Zero Trust Exchange Platform to Deliver Zero Trust for Workloads
summary: Zscaler announced the general availability of its new Workload Communications solution, extending Zero Trust security to workloads and applications in public clouds. This solution aims to simplify multi-cloud workload connectivity, eliminate attack surfaces, and enhance application performance by moving away from traditional VPNs and firewalls. It provides Zero Trust for cloud workloads across cloud-to-internet, cloud-to-cloud, cloud-to-data center, and intra-cloud communications.

title: Department of Justice announces settlement with Microsoft over immigration discrimination claims
summary: The US Department of Justice (DoJ) has settled with Microsoft Corporation regarding claims of discrimination against non-US citizen employees, including lawful permanent residents, refugees, and asylees. Microsoft was found to have unlawfully required these individuals to prove a need for visa sponsorship and to provide unnecessary work authorization documents. As part of the settlement, Microsoft will reform its hiring processes, pay civil penalties, and be subject to monitoring.

title: How much control should Apple have over your iPhone and the App Store?
summary: Apple is facing increasing scrutiny over its tight control of the App Store, which critics call a monopoly due to its exclusive app distribution, mandatory commissions, and content restrictions. While Apple argues these measures ensure user security and privacy, lawmakers and regulators worldwide are pushing for changes to increase competition, potentially leading to more app choices and lower prices for consumers, but also raising concerns about security. Despite some minor concessions, Apple largely maintains its stance, suggesting significant shifts may only occur if forced by new legislation or legal challenges.

title: DXC Technology Enables Copa Airlines’ Transformation by Modernizing and Migrating Passenger Service System with Cloud Right™ Approach
summary: DXC Technology announced a multiyear renewal with Copa Airlines to modernize its mainframe-based Passenger Service System (PSS) and migrate it entirely to the public cloud using DXC's Cloud Right™ approach. This initiative, in collaboration with Microsoft, aims to accelerate Copa's digital transformation by providing a flexible, scalable, and open airline core IT platform, improving customer and staff experience. The migration to Microsoft Azure is expected to increase integration scalability and reduce costs, offering greater flexibility for future development and continuous modernization of PSS components.

title: Gartner Forecasts Worldwide IT Spending to Exceed $4 Trillion in 2022
summary: Gartner projects global IT spending to reach $4.5 trillion in 2022, a 5.5% increase from 2021. This growth is driven by digital transformation initiatives, with enterprise software expected to have the highest growth. In Thailand, IT spending is forecast to increase by 6.4% to THB 871.5 billion in 2022, also led by enterprise software growth.

title: Microsoft and Objective help government agencies balance collaboration with information governance
summary: Microsoft and Objective Corporation have partnered to help government agencies and regulated industries manage collaboration and information governance. Their agreement ensures that information shared in hybrid digital environments, particularly within Microsoft 365 applications like Teams, SharePoint, and Outlook, adheres to strict compliance and data governance standards. This collaboration aims to provide robust record-keeping and regulatory compliance without impeding user productivity, which is crucial for public sector and highly regulated entities adopting hybrid work models.

title: NFL's Raiders use analytics to engage new customer base
summary: The NFL's Las Vegas Raiders modernized their analytics stack to understand and engage a new customer base after moving from Oakland. They partnered with Data Clymer to build a cloud-based system using Salesforce, Matillion, Snowflake, and Tableau to process and analyze customer data. This new system allows the Raiders to rapidly gain insights, develop targeted marketing campaigns, and maximize diverse revenue opportunities from their new stadium in Las Vegas, which operates as a tourist destination.

title: IBM and MuleSoft Announce Global Relationship to Help Accelerate Flexibility Across Public and Private Clouds
summary: IBM and MuleSoft have formed a global relationship to accelerate flexibility across public and private clouds, focusing on modernizing applications and integrating systems. MuleSoft plans to extend its Anypoint Runtime Fabric to run on Red Hat OpenShift, enhancing deployment options for APIs, integrations, and automations. The collaboration will also boost real-time integrations for IBM Z customers, particularly in financial services, and IBM Consulting will increase its MuleSoft-certified professionals to support digital transformation.

title: Microsoft Expands Azure Space Partnerships with Azure Orbital Preview
summary: Microsoft unveiled a public preview of Azure Orbital, its groundstation-as-a-service offering for satellite communication and data processing, emphasizing its integration with Azure's hyperscale computing resources. The company is expanding its Azure Orbital network through new partnerships, including ST Engineering iDirect for virtualized modems and an enhanced collaboration with KSAT for groundstation access. Additionally, Microsoft announced new partnerships with Airbus for satellite imagery integration into Azure Maps and Blackshark.ai, Esri, and Orbital Insight for geospatial intelligence and data analytics solutions within Azure.

title: Electronic Arts Inc. stock falls Thursday, underperforms market
summary: Shares of Electronic Arts Inc. (EA) fell 1.08% to $125.00 on Thursday, underperforming the broader market as the S&P 500 Index and Dow Jones Industrial Average also declined. The stock closed $25.30 below its 52-week high and also underperformed competitors like Microsoft Corp. and Walt Disney Co. Trading volume was below its 50-day average.

title: NetApp appoints chief product officer who doesn’t look after all products
summary: NetApp has appointed Harvinder (Harv) Bhela as its first chief product officer, who will oversee most, but not all, of NetApp's products. Anthony Lye will continue to lead the Cloud Management and Platform Services Business Unit, specifically focusing on CloudOps, while Bhela will handle cloud storage, data services, and hybrid cloud businesses. This dual leadership aims to accelerate the company's pivot to cloud while maintaining leadership in flash and object storage.

title: Pure Storage Takes On Tier 1 Storage With FlashArray//XL
summary: Pure Storage has launched its new FlashArray//XL family, comprising the XL130 and XL170 models, to target the high-end, mission-critical storage market previously dominated by companies like Dell EMC. These new systems are designed to provide cloud-like scalability and flexibility in on-premises datacenters, offering significant improvements in IOPS, effective capacity, and density compared to previous FlashArray//X systems. This move aims to fill a gap in Pure Storage's portfolio and challenge competitors for the most demanding enterprise workloads like SAP HANA and Oracle databases.

title: Microsoft shoppers get another BNPL option
summary: Microsoft is expanding its partnership with Citizens Bank to offer a new buy now-pay later (BNPL) option for shoppers in the Microsoft Store, allowing them to finance larger purchases like laptops and Xbox consoles over 12 or 18 months with no interest. This initiative builds on Citizens' existing financing for Microsoft's Xbox All Access Program and caters to the growing consumer demand for flexible payment options, especially as e-commerce continues to rise. The move comes as BNPL transactions are projected to increase significantly and more financial institutions are entering the space, highlighting the shift towards "industrial-grade" BNPL solutions for merchants.

title: Cloudflare announces integrations with MDM companies
summary: Cloudflare announced new integrations with Mobile Device Management (MDM) vendors such as Microsoft Intune, Ivanti, JumpCloud, Kandji, and Hexnode. These partnerships aim to simplify the deployment and management of Cloudflare WARP, its Zero Trust security platform, across diverse device fleets. The article highlights the importance of MDM solutions for organizations managing dispersed workforces and sensitive data, and how Cloudflare's integrations streamline security for enterprise applications.

title: How ConocoPhillips is opening an innovation treasure trove
summary: ConocoPhillips is fostering a culture of innovation, led by Director Liz Jolley, to drive success and adapt to a changing industry. The company utilizes its "Fuel" software platform to facilitate global collaboration, allowing employees to share ideas and adopt proven solutions. This approach has led to significant improvements in operations, cost reduction, and problem-solving across various business units worldwide.

title: 4 Charts on Apple's $3 Trillion Market Cap
summary: Apple Inc. has become the first company to achieve a $3 trillion market capitalization, briefly hitting $182.88 per share. This article highlights the immense scale of Apple's market cap through various comparisons, such as its value exceeding the total market cap of all public companies in Canada. It also discusses Apple's dominance within the U.S. market, making up nearly 22% of all U.S.-domiciled technology companies' total market capitalization.

title: Why Oracle’s stock is surging to an all-time high
summary: Oracle's stock surged nearly 16% to an all-time high after strong earnings and guidance, driven by its license business and improved cloud performance. The company's strategy of deeply integrating hardware and software and investing in next-gen cloud has been key to its success, particularly in its Fusion ERP business. While skeptics question the true cloud momentum due to reporting methods, market watchers note Oracle's strong performance compared to competitors like SAP and IBM.

title: Apache Log4j Vulnerability - Check Point Blog
summary: This article from Check Point Research details the critical Log4j vulnerability (CVE-2021-44228), a remote code execution exploit impacting a vast number of Java-based applications globally. It explains the nature of the vulnerability, the rapid evolution of exploit variations, and the immediate protective measures offered by Check Point's Infinity Platform. The piece also confirms that Check Point's own architecture is not affected and provides guidance on mitigation and continued support.

title: Healthcare Triangle (HCTI) Acquires DevCool, an Electronic
summary: Healthcare Triangle (HCTI) announced the acquisition of DevCool, an EHR-focused healthcare IT and managed services company, a move expected to add approximately $20 million in revenues. This acquisition aims to strengthen HCTI's leadership in healthcare IT by improving patient care, reducing IT costs, and accelerating EHR deployments, especially for cloud hosting. The combined entity plans to leverage cloud technologies to enhance clinical, operational, and financial performance for healthcare providers and integrate DevCool’s client base with HCTI’s SaaS platforms.

title: SnapLogic raises $165M to accelerate enterprise automation via data integration
summary: SnapLogic, an enterprise automation firm specializing in data integration, has secured $165 million in a funding round led by Sixth Street Growth, valuing the company at $1 billion. These new funds will support international expansion, sales and marketing growth, and product innovation. SnapLogic's cloud-based platform uses "Snaps" (pre-packaged software connectors) and AI to help companies like Adobe, Siemens, and Workday integrate disparate applications and automate data workflows, leading to increased efficiency and reduced costs.

title: Top 25 DOD Execs to Watch in 2021: Microsoft’s Angela Heise
summary: Angela Heise, Corporate Vice President of Defense & Intelligence at Microsoft, is highlighted as a top DOD executive to watch in 2021. With over 20 years of experience, Heise is focused on helping defense and intelligence agencies globally advance their missions by leveraging Microsoft's technology to manage data, derive insights, and accelerate innovation amidst evolving threats and a global pandemic. Microsoft aims to be a trusted partner in transforming how governments achieve their missions.

title: Microsoft (MSFT) Changes Logo & Name for Xbox Game Pass for PC
summary: Microsoft has rebranded its Xbox Game Pass for PC to "PC Game Pass" and updated its logo. This change comes as Microsoft actively expands its video game business, focusing on its successful Game Pass subscription service, which now boasts over 18 million users. The company is also growing its cloud gaming service, while facing increasing competition in the lucrative gaming market, notably from Sony, which is reportedly developing a similar subscription offering.

title: SiriusXM Names Joseph Inzerillo Chief Product & Technology Officer
summary: SiriusXM has appointed Joseph Inzerillo as its new Chief Product & Technology Officer, effective January 10, 2022. Inzerillo, a veteran of MLB and Disney's streaming services, will be responsible for defining and implementing SiriusXM's product roadmap, satellite infrastructure, and technology strategy. He will lead a large team to enhance capabilities, improve customer experience, and drive innovation across all platforms.

title: Perion Network Announces Closing of $180.0 Million Follow-on Offering of Ordinary Shares, Including Full Exercise of Underwriters’ Option to Purchase Additional Shares
summary: Perion Network Ltd. announced the closing of its $180.0 million follow-on public offering, which included the full exercise of the underwriters’ option to purchase additional shares. A total of 8,372,092 ordinary shares were sold at $21.50 per share, generating aggregate gross proceeds of $180.0 million to the Company. Perion intends to use the net proceeds for working capital, business growth including potential mergers or acquisitions, and general corporate purposes.

title: TeraWulf Is Attracting A-List Investors For Its Sustainable Bitcoin Solution
summary: TeraWulf, a company focused on environmentally-friendly Bitcoin mining, is attracting A-list investors due to its sustainable approach. Notable investors like Gwyneth Paltrow, Mindy Kaling, and Sara Foster have joined, supporting TeraWulf's goal of achieving 100% zero-carbon emissions in its operations by leveraging nuclear, hydro, and solar power. The company aims to address environmental concerns associated with cryptocurrency mining and is preparing for a public debut to expand its substantial mining capacity.

title: BlackRock Future U.S. Themes ETF ETF Price, Holdings, & News (NYSEARCA:BTHM)
summary: The BlackRock Future U.S. Themes ETF (BTHM) is an actively managed ETF launched on December 14, 2021, focusing on US stocks that provide exposure to emerging and structural themes. As of May 4, 2026, it trades at $40.71, reflecting a 5.6% increase since January 2026, and has assets under management of $7.89 million with a net expense ratio of 0.60%. Its top holdings include NVIDIA, Apple, and Microsoft.

title: What Zoom’s $85m class action lawsuit means for data privacy
summary: Zoom has agreed to pay an $85 million settlement in a class action lawsuit alleging it shared user data without consent and falsely claimed end-to-end encryption. This case highlights a broader data privacy movement forcing companies to increase transparency and adjust to stricter regulations. Experts believe the lawsuit serves as a cautionary tale for the digital ecosystem and will prompt other companies to re-evaluate their data protection policies.

title: Before the Billions: The First Jobs of Some of the Richest Men in the World
summary: This article explores the humble beginnings of some of the world's wealthiest individuals, highlighting their first jobs before achieving billionaire status. It details the early career paths of 15 billionaires, from Travis Kalanick selling knives door-to-door to Jeff Bezos working as a McDonald's fry cook, demonstrating that even the richest people started with ordinary or unconventional jobs. The piece also includes advice on how readers can work towards boosting their own net worth.

title: Research at Microsoft 2021: Collaborating for real-world change
summary: This article details Microsoft Research's 2021 initiatives, emphasizing a shift towards addressing global challenges like climate change, healthcare equity, and digital divides through collaborative innovation. It highlights advancements in AI, such as large language models and computer vision, and showcases efforts in fostering hybrid work, enabling accessibility, and promoting societal resilience and sustainability. The report also underscores the importance of trustworthy AI development, privacy preservation, and engaging with the global research community through fellowships and partnerships.

title: The Invesco QQQ Stock Price Is Up 23.7% Since January. Could There Be More Gains?
summary: The Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ: QQQ) has seen its stock price rise 23.7% since January, driven by major tech companies like Apple and Google, despite recent pullbacks. Investors are closely watching the Federal Reserve's monetary policy meeting for potential hawkish policies that could further impact the Nasdaq index and the QQQ ETF. While the ETF is currently in a downtrend, its present stock price may be attractive for a future rally, though a clear upward trend based on EMA crossings is yet to materialize.

title: Vertical Aerospace Lists on NYSE Following Merger with Broadstone Acquisition Corp.
summary: Vertical Aerospace announced the closing of its business combination with Broadstone Acquisition Corp. and its listing on the NYSE under the ticker EVTL. The company aims to pioneer zero-carbon aviation with its VX4 electric aircraft, backed by significant funding and pre-orders from major airlines, targeting certification by 2024. This milestone marks a significant step towards commercial operations in the mid-2020s, with strong support from key partners and investors.

title: Gtmhub raises $120M to help companies manage business initiatives
summary: Gtmhub, a startup providing a platform for managing business initiatives using the OKRs approach, has raised $120 million in funding led by Index Ventures. This funding round is reportedly the largest ever in the OKRs enterprise software segment, bringing their total raised to $161 million. The company plans to use the capital to expand its market presence, double its headcount, and triple its revenues within the next year.

title: Microsoft named a Leader in 2021 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Cloud DBMS Platforms
summary: Microsoft has been recognized as a Leader in the 2021 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Cloud Database Management Systems, highlighting its strong execution and comprehensive vision. This achievement is attributed to Microsoft's continuous innovation and integration of a robust data portfolio into its cloud data ecosystem. The company emphasizes its end-to-end data platform, offering limitless database performance, unmatched analytics, and unified data governance to support digital transformations for businesses.

title: Desktop computers and All-in-One PCs
summary: HP offers a wide range of desktop computers and All-in-One PCs designed for various uses, including work, entertainment, gaming, and creative tasks. The article highlights new AI PC models like the HP OmniDesk and OmniStudio X, alongside established lines such as HP Pavilion, Envy, OMEN, and VICTUS, detailing their specifications and intended applications. Customers can filter choices by use case, series, operating system, product type, and screen size to find the perfect device.

title: Where Are the Best Places for Women to Work? Mainly in Tech
summary: A new survey by Comparably reveals that six of the top ten best companies for women to work at in the U.S. are in the technology sector. IBM Corp. was ranked as the top large company for women, with Adobe Inc., HubSpot, Inc., Medallia Inc., Microsoft Corp., and The Knot Worldwide Inc. also making the list from the tech industry. The rankings are based on ratings provided by female users between November 2020 and November 2021.

title: Focus: Boeing wants to build its next airplane in the 'metaverse'
summary: Boeing is launching an ambitious strategy to integrate a digital ecosystem for designing, producing, and servicing its aircraft, utilizing technologies like immersive 3-D engineering and HoloLens headsets. This "metaverse" approach aims to improve quality, safety, and efficiency, preventing issues like those encountered with the 737 MAX and 787 Dreamliner. While facing challenges and skepticism due to past technological hurdles and R&D cuts, Boeing believes this digital transformation is crucial for its future aircraft programs and competitive edge against rivals like Airbus.

title: Cerner could be acquired by Oracle, says WSJ
summary: Oracle is reportedly in talks to acquire health IT giant Cerner Corp. for an estimated $30 billion, which would be Oracle's largest acquisition to date. This move would significantly bolster Oracle's presence in healthcare technology, particularly in cloud computing and AI, following a trend of major tech companies investing heavily in healthcare-focused firms. The potential acquisition comes amidst a challenging year for Cerner, despite its CEO expressing optimism about long-term growth.

title: Should you invest in Google?
summary: This article analyzes Alphabet (Google) as a potential investment, highlighting its market dominance in search, strong financial performance, and diversified segments including Google Services, Google Cloud, and "Other Bets" (moonshots). It discusses the company's profitability, challenges like competition and the rise of the Metaverse, and valuation metrics, concluding that while Alphabet has strong fundamentals, investors should monitor its growth trajectory and margins. The article also explains the different share classes (GOOGL and GOOG).

title: Investor Alert for Week Ended December 17, 2021
summary: This investor alert discusses the emerging metaverse, Web 3.0, and its potential to revolutionize various sectors including social interaction, commerce, and gaming, comparing its disruptive potential to the early internet. It covers investment opportunities in hardware, software, NFTs, and virtual real estate within this digital ecosystem. Additionally, the report provides an overview of performance and opportunities in airline, emerging markets, energy & natural resources, domestic equities, and crypto sectors, alongside a gold market update.

title: Verizon, T-Mobile Shun Public Clouds for Network Infrastructure
summary: Verizon and T-Mobile are opting against using public clouds for their core network functions, choosing instead to rely on private, in-house cloud platforms. This strategy is driven by the need for extreme reliability and security for critical services, a stance reinforced by recent Amazon Web Services outages. In contrast, AT&T is moving its 5G core and network workloads entirely to Microsoft Azure.

title: Weekly Roundup: What We’ve Learned About the Log4j Vulnerability
summary: This article summarizes the critical Log4j vulnerability, CVE-2021-44228, also known as "Log4Shell," identifying it as one of the most severe in a decade due to its widespread use in Java projects and high exploitability. It details how the exploit works, the types of attacks observed, and provides guidance for mitigation and strengthening security posture through zero trust network architectures and deception technologies. The piece stresses the long-term impact of this vulnerability on security teams.

title: At Waters, a digital workplace strategy pays off amid crisis
summary: Waters Corp. CIO Brook Colangelo's decision to migrate the company to cloud-based productivity and collaboration software before the coronavirus pandemic proved prescient, enabling its 7,000 employees to stay connected and secure while working from home. This digital workplace strategy, supported by a modified Spotify "squad" model, improved the employee experience and allowed the company to handle an increased volume of online engagements and Microsoft Teams usage during the crisis. Colangelo emphasizes thinking like a platform leader, adopting a growth mindset, and obsessing over user adoption for a successful digital workplace.

title: Amazon silenced criticism of Xi to do business in China: Report
summary: A Reuters report alleges that Amazon.com Inc. quieted criticism of President Xi Jinping's book on its Chinese platform to maintain business in China. This involved scrubbing negative ratings and reviews for "The Governance of China" following requests from Beijing. This situation mirrors cases of other US companies like Apple and contrasts with others like Yahoo! and LinkedIn that have exited the Chinese market due to a challenging business environment.

title: Oracle snags Cerner in $28B mega deal to make a big move into healthcare
summary: Oracle announced its acquisition of electronic healthcare records company Cerner for approximately $28.3 billion, a move designed to significantly bolster Oracle's presence in the healthcare vertical and expand its cloud infrastructure business. This acquisition represents Oracle's largest to date and aligns with its strategy for substantial revenue growth by penetrating a fast-growing industry. The deal faces potential regulatory scrutiny, similar to Microsoft's recent healthcare acquisition, but Cerner's CEO sees it as an opportunity to accelerate EHR modernization and improve patient care.

title: India's USD10 billion chip incentive: Which Singapore companies may jump in
summary: India has introduced a USD 10 billion incentive plan to attract global semiconductor and display manufacturers, with companies like Israel's Tower Semiconductor, Taiwan's Foxconn, and a Singaporean consortium reportedly interested. This initiative is part of Prime Minister Modi's "Make in India" plan to boost manufacturing's contribution to GDP and create high-quality jobs, reducing reliance on imports. Singapore, a significant player in the semiconductor industry outside the "big four" in Asia, hosts major foreign and local chip makers, some of which may leverage this opportunity in India.

title: 5 things to know about Oracle after $28.3 billion acquisition of Kansas City’s Cerner
summary: Oracle has announced a $28.3 billion acquisition of Cerner Corp., Kansas City's largest private employer, marking one of the year's biggest deals. This move signifies Oracle's growing push into the healthcare industry, following similar expansions by other tech giants. The acquisition brings together Oracle, an $280 billion company with 133,000 employees globally, and Cerner, valued at $23 billion with 28,000 employees worldwide, notably 13,000 in Kansas City.

title: Oracle to acquire Cerner in $28.3B deal
summary: Oracle announced its acquisition of medical record technology provider Cerner in an all-cash deal valued at $28.3 billion, or $95 per share. This strategic move aims to expand Oracle's presence in the healthcare sector and boost its cloud business globally, with the transaction expected to close in 2022. Oracle CEO Safra Catz anticipates the deal will be a significant revenue growth engine, while chairman Larry Ellison highlighted the potential to reduce administrative burdens for medical professionals and improve patient care.

title: The Metaverse Is a $1 Trillion Revenue Opportunity. Here’s How to Invest
summary: The metaverse, a new iteration of the internet, is projected to be a trillion-dollar revenue opportunity, transforming how people work, play, socialize, and invest. This emerging digital ecosystem will feature virtual reality experiences, digital assets like NFTs, and virtual real estate, attracting interest from major tech companies, luxury brands, and investors. Early investment opportunities exist in hardware, software, and platforms operating within this evolving virtual world.

title: Telenet enters into one-year extension of agreement with Liberty Global for Horizon 4 video platform and Horizon Go application
summary: Telenet Group Holding NV announced a one-year extension of its agreement with Liberty Global Technology Services BV for the Horizon 4 video platform and Horizon Go application, maintaining the same terms and conditions as the previous agreement. This extension, estimated to cost Telenet EUR 20.4 million, allows the company to continue offering a high-end, feature-rich video platform to its customers until December 31, 2022. The transaction was approved by the committee of independent directors and the statutory auditor, who found it to be in the company's interest and consistent with market practice.

title: Eating to Win: Scott Hemphill spotlights an antitrust problem for highly innovative industries: anticompetitive acquisitions of nascent competitors
summary: NYU Law Professor Scott Hemphill and Columbia Law Professor Tim Wu argue for stronger antitrust enforcement against large companies acquiring nascent competitors with innovative potential, even if their competitive threat isn't fully realized yet. Their paper, "Nascent Competitors," highlights how such acquisitions can be anticompetitive, especially in fast-moving industries, using examples like the Visa-Plaid merger attempt. They suggest regulators examine patterns of acquisitions and substantial overpayment for acquired firms, and consider ex-post enforcement, emphasizing that the harm from unchecked anticompetitive acquisitions outweighs concerns about chilling startup investments.

title: ST Going for Style
summary: STMicroelectronics is leveraging its laser beam scanning (LBS) technology to enable fashionable and lightweight smart augmented reality (AR) glasses, crucial for mass consumer adoption. The global market for smart AR glasses is projected to grow significantly, and ST's LBS offers advantages in size, weight, power efficiency, and resolution over competing technologies. ST has also formed the LaSAR Alliance to accelerate the design and manufacture of AR wearable devices.

title: Oracle to buy Cerner for $28.3 bln in healthcare sector push
summary: Oracle announced its acquisition of Cerner for $28.3 billion, marking its largest deal ever and a significant push into the healthcare sector. This acquisition gives Oracle access to a vast amount of healthcare data, which it plans to leverage for its AI-based cloud services and to migrate Cerner's software to its own cloud platform. The deal is expected to close in 2022 and contribute to Oracle's revenue growth and earnings.

title: AT&T Sells Xandr Ad Business to Microsoft for $1 Billion
summary: AT&T Inc. has agreed to sell its Xandr digital advertising division to Microsoft Corp. for approximately $1 billion. This sale marks AT&T's retreat from the digital ad market, as it deemed Xandr non-core to its operations after seeking a buyer for over a year. The acquisition will allow customers on Microsoft's properties, like MSN, to access Xandr's automated online advertising marketplace.

title: ‘Spider-Man’ $260 million debut smashes pandemic-era record
summary: “Spider-Man: No Way Home” shattered pandemic-era box office records with a $260.1 million debut in North America, marking the second-highest domestic opening weekend of all time. This success, driven by a core demographic of 18-to-34-year-old fans, offers hope for the theater industry's recovery in 2022, despite ongoing challenges like the Omicron variant and uneven audience return. Sony's decision for a theatrical-only release underscored the cultural impact of exclusive cinematic experiences.

title: Entertainment Robots Market to Witness Huge Growth by 2026 | Aldebaran Robotics, Blu Frog Robotics, Hasbro
summary: This press release announces a comprehensive study on the global Entertainment Robots market, forecasting significant growth by 2026. The report by AMA Research & Media LLP provides insights into key players, market trends, drivers, and opportunities, highlighting the entertainment industry's increasing adoption of automation. It details market segmentation by type, application, component, and end-user, covering regions globally.

title: 15 Best Windows 10 Themes
summary: This article lists the 15 best Windows 10 themes, offering various options to personalize a PC's desktop. It provides detailed instructions on how to install themes through Microsoft Store or third-party sources and highlights diverse themes ranging from 3D designs and anime to classic operating system looks and pop culture references like Star Wars and NBA. The article emphasizes that changing themes is a simple yet effective way to customize one's device and reflect personal interests.

title: Xandr, Formerly AppNexus, Is Now Formerly AT&T, After Its Acquisition By Microsoft
summary: AT&T has sold its ad tech business, Xandr (formerly AppNexus), to Microsoft, marking the end of AppNexus's unsuccessful integration within AT&T. Despite AT&T's vision for advertising as a key business pillar, AppNexus struggled to find its place, burdened by legacy ad businesses and internal challenges regarding data privacy. Microsoft, an early investor and long-time client of AppNexus, is seen as a logical new home for the company's technology and engineering talent, aiming to accelerate its digital advertising and retail media solutions.

title: AT&T to Sell Xandr Advertising Business to Microsoft
summary: AT&T is selling its Xandr global advertising business to Microsoft, continuing the telecom giant's strategy of divesting content-related assets. Microsoft stated that Xandr complements its current advertising offerings, while AT&T aims to deleverage and focus on its core data business. This sale is part of CEO John Stankey's efforts to undo prior large acquisitions and pivot away from the content creation and monetization segments.

title: AT&T sells Xandr ad business to Microsoft for $1 billion
summary: AT&T has sold its Xandr digital advertising business to Microsoft for an estimated $1 billion. This divestiture is part of AT&T's broader strategy to scale back its media operations, following moves with DirecTV and WarnerMedia. The sale allows Microsoft to integrate Xandr's platform into its properties, enhancing its online advertising capabilities.

title: Microsoft acquires AT&T’s Xandr unit to grow its advertising business
summary: Microsoft has acquired AT&T's Xandr advertising technology unit, expanding its presence in the digital advertising market, especially into TV ads. This acquisition, along with a reported partnership with Taboola, will intensify competition with dominant players like Google and Meta. Xandr provides cloud services for buying and measuring TV ad campaigns, and its integration could significantly boost Microsoft's advertising revenue by leveraging its extensive enterprise customer base.

title: AT&T to Sell Digital Ad Tech Platform Xandr to Microsoft
summary: AT&T will sell its digital advertising platform Xandr to Microsoft, marking the end of AT&T's efforts to compete in the online advertising market. Microsoft stated that Xandr's digital ad marketplace will enhance its digital advertising and retail media capabilities. Financial terms of the deal were not disclosed.

title: AT&T to sell Xandr ad unit to Microsoft
summary: AT&T announced it is selling its advertising unit, Xandr, to Microsoft, partly exiting a venture that had proven expensive for the telecom company. This sale aligns with AT&T's efforts to reduce debt amidst its broader strategy shifts, including the pending WarnerMedia-Discovery Inc deal. For Microsoft, the acquisition aims to accelerate its digital advertising and retail media solutions.

title: Apple’s long-term credit rating upgraded to AAA by Moody’s
summary: Moody’s Investors Service upgraded Apple Inc.’s long-term credit rating to Aaa, placing it in an exclusive group with Microsoft and Johnson & Johnson as the only U.S. S&P 500 corporations with the highest possible credit score. This upgrade reflects Apple's exceptional liquidity, robust earnings, and strong business profile, as the company continues to focus on a net cash-neutral position and expand into new markets like augmented reality and cars. Despite potential chip-related supply shortages impacting revenue, investors remain optimistic about Apple's long-term prospects.

title: Oracle Cerner Acquisition Opens the Door for Deeper Inroads into the Healthcare Data Business
summary: Oracle has announced its acquisition of Cerner Corp for $28.3 billion, marking its largest deal to date and signifying a major push into the healthcare data business. This strategic move aims to solidify Oracle's presence in the cloud and healthcare sectors, leveraging Cerner's electronic medical records expertise and addressing the rising demand for cloud-based healthcare solutions. The acquisition is viewed as a power move that allows Oracle to compete more effectively with other tech giants in the cloud arena while enabling Cerner to continue its transformation and growth.

title: Moody's gives Apple top 'AAA' credit rating on growth promise
summary: Ratings agency Moody's upgraded Apple Inc.'s long-term credit rating to 'AAA' with a stable outlook, citing its exceptional liquidity and robust earnings. This places Apple in an elite group of companies with the highest rating. While Apple's financial performance was strong in fiscal 2021, the company faces execution risks from short product cycles, shifting consumer preferences, and supply chain management.

title: Procore Appoints Microsoft Executive Erin Chapple to Board of Directors
summary: Procore Technologies, Inc. announced the appointment of Microsoft Executive Erin Chapple to its Board of Directors. Chapple, Corporate Vice President of Azure Core, will provide crucial insights into Procore's platform strategy and architecture. Her extensive experience in technology and leadership, including two decades at Microsoft, is expected to help Procore enhance its platform and connect the construction industry.

title: Market Breadth Showcases Equal-Weight Benefits
summary: The article discusses the benefits of equal-weight strategies in investing, particularly highlighted by current market breadth where a few large-cap tech stocks are dominating the S&P 500. It suggests that while cap-weighted indices show strong performance due to these few stocks, equal-weight ETFs like RSP offer better diversification and can outperform when market leadership narrows, as demonstrated by its recent performance against the S&P 500.

title: OpenText Closes Zix Corporation Acquisition
summary: OpenText announced the completion of its acquisition of Zix Corporation for approximately C$860 million. This acquisition aims to expand OpenText's SMB platform for data protection, threat management, email security, and compliance solutions. OpenText expects Zix to be accretive to organic growth and margin dollars within 12-18 months of integration.

title: Virtual Guns in Videogames Could Soon Be Worth Real Money
summary: Videogame makers are increasingly adopting Non-Fungible Tokens (NFTs) for in-game items like weapons and gear, transforming them into potentially valuable, tradable assets for players. This trend, exemplified by Ubisoft's recent NFT giveaway in "Tom Clancy's Ghost Recon Breakpoint," allows gamers to trade and resell virtual items, a significant shift from traditional in-game purchases. While extending the reach of digital deeds, this move has also caused some controversy among players.

title: 32% of Growth to Originate from APAC for Data Analytics Market|Evolving Opportunities with Amazon Web Services Inc., International Business Machines Corp. & Microsoft Corp. |17000+ Technavio Reports
summary: The data analytics market is projected to grow by USD 196.47 billion from 2021 to 2026, with a CAGR of 13.54%. A significant 32% of this growth is expected to come from the APAC region, particularly from China and India. The market's expansion is driven by the extensive use of modern technology in company operations, though challenges like integrating data from various sources may temper growth.

title: Boeing Wants to Build its Next Airplane in the 'Metaverse'
summary: Boeing plans to revolutionize its aircraft manufacturing by uniting design, production, and services under a single digital system, aiming to build its next airplane in the "metaverse" within the next two years. This digital transformation, involving 3-D designs, robots, and mixed reality headsets, seeks to improve quality, safety, and efficiency while reducing design-related issues. The initiative also comes as the company tries to regain trust after the 737 MAX crisis and avoid future manufacturing problems like those encountered with the 787 Dreamliner.

title: KKR to Acquire Leading Software Provider Yayoi from ORIX
summary: KKR has announced a definitive agreement to acquire Yayoi Co., Ltd., a leading software provider for small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Japan, from ORIX Corporation. Yayoi is Japan's largest financial and accounting software provider for SMEs, with over 2.5 million registered users and a strong track record of digital transformation support. KKR aims to leverage its global expertise in technology and software businesses to further penetrate the Japanese market and promote Yayoi's growth, with the transaction expected to close by March 1, 2022.

title: Shed Concentration Risk With Equal-Weight ETFs
summary: This article discusses the increasing concentration risk in cap-weighted indexes like the S&P 500, primarily due to the large market capitalization of a few tech giants like Apple and Microsoft. It advocates for equal-weight exchange-traded funds (ETFs), such as the Invesco S&P 500 Equal Weight ETF (RSP), as a solution to provide comparable returns with superior diversification. The article highlights how equal-weight ETFs mitigate the risks associated with an over-reliance on a few mega-cap stocks.

title: Shun Concentration Risk With Equal-Weight ETFs
summary: This article discusses the increasing concentration risk in cap-weighted S&P 500 indexes due to the massive market capitalization of a few tech giants like Apple and Microsoft. It promotes equal-weight ETFs, such as the Invesco S&P 500 Equal Weight ETF (RSP), as a solution to this problem, highlighting their comparable performance with superior diversification. The piece draws historical parallels to the tech bubble, emphasizing the benefits of a less concentrated portfolio.

title: Social Media Company Quora Is Going Public: Here Are the Details
summary: Quora is considering going public, potentially following other social media companies like Reddit, Rumble, and TMTG. While no IPO date has been set, Reuters reported Quora could go public in 2022 with a valuation of $4 billion, a significant increase from its 2019 private funding. The company generates revenue through advertising and subscription products, aiming to become free-cash-flow-positive on ad revenue alone.

title: Returnship initiatives are having a remarkable impact on women
summary: This article highlights the significant positive impact of "returnship" programs on women re-entering the workforce after a break, using Kaustubha Vecham Shravan's inspiring journey through VMware's Taara program as an example. While these initiatives are highly effective, a Zinnov study reveals that less than 2% of women who leave India Inc. manage to reintegrate through structured programs, emphasizing the need for more scalable and business-aligned returnship opportunities. Morgan Stanley's successful program in India is presented as a model, demonstrating how linking selection to specific job roles and providing comprehensive support can lead to high retention and valuable contributions from returning women.

title: Legal tech buzzed throughout 2021 with IPOs, new 'unicorns'
summary: The legal technology sector experienced significant growth in 2021 with several companies going public, including LegalZoom.com Inc, CS Disco Inc, and Intapp Inc. Investors also poured capital into private legal tech companies, leading to at least two, Clio and Everlaw Inc, achieving "unicorn" status with valuations exceeding $1 billion. This activity signals a maturation of the legal tech market, driven partly by increased technology adoption due to COVID-19.

title: Google Cloud Pricing: The Complete Guide
summary: This comprehensive guide details the pricing models for Google Cloud Platform services, including compute, storage, networking, SQL, and serverless options. It covers pay-as-you-go, long-term commitments, and free tier options, highlighting various pricing factors and potential cost-saving strategies. The article also touches upon NetApp Cloud Volumes ONTAP as a solution for optimizing Google Cloud costs through storage efficiencies.

title: DXC Technology Co. stock falls Friday, underperforms market
summary: DXC Technology Co. (DXC) stock fell 0.62% to $32.19 on Friday, underperforming the broader market as both the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average also declined. This marked the fourth consecutive day of losses for the stock, placing it significantly below its 52-week high. The company's performance was mixed compared to competitors like Microsoft and IBM, which also saw declines, while Accenture rose slightly.
